Prepare the complete Rolex, gather records and spare links, and leave repairs or polishing until after an initial discussion. At the evaluation, confirm what is being examined, what the offer includes and how an agreed sale will be completed.

In this guide

  • 1. Make a simple item record
  • 2. Gather the complete package
  • 3. Preserve its current condition
  • 4. Agree on the examination
  • 5. Compare the amount and its conditions
  • 6. Confirm payment before the handover

1. Make a simple item record

Write down the model or reference shown in your records, the accessories you have and any known damage or alterations. If you do not know the reference or production date, say so. A remembered purchase year should not become an unsupported manufacturing date.

The official Rolex collections can help you recognize model-family names. Current catalogue images cannot establish an older watch's exact reference, originality, authenticity or purchase value.

Record the watch's present condition for your own records. Avoid publicly sharing full identifying numbers or personal details from warranty documents when seeking an initial conversation.

2. Gather the complete package

Include spare bracelet links, the box, warranty papers, receipts and service invoices if available. Keep unrelated accessories separate. Missing papers do not prevent you from asking for a purchase evaluation.

For an inherited watch, keep family information distinct from documented history and confirm your authority to decide about a sale. The vintage Rolex guide covers uncertain history and component originality.

3. Preserve its current condition

Do not open the case, force the crown or arrange cosmetic restoration just to prepare for an offer. If the watch is damaged or has stopped, describe that before visiting. Ask whether an as-is evaluation is appropriate before spending money on repairs.

Rolex's manufacturer guidance provides care and servicing information. The condition of an individual older watch still matters; a general cleaning instruction should not be treated as proof it is currently water-resistant.

4. Agree on the examination

Ask who will handle the watch, whether opening or additional testing is proposed, and how any time away from you will be documented. Get an itemized receipt if the watch must be left for further work.

A purchase proposal is not automatically a formal authentication report. Rolex Certified Pre-Owned is a separate manufacturer programme, not a generic label for every used Rolex evaluation.

5. Compare the amount and its conditions

Ask for the offered amount and the precise items included. Note any unresolved inspection condition, charge or expiration of the proposal. Compare another offer on the same basis if you want a second opinion.

For a gold Rolex, request consideration as a complete watch before a metal-only calculation. The gold Rolex guide explains why case and bracelet materials do not replace reference-level evaluation.

For a Day-Date, the reference and bracelet evaluation guide explains which details and records to bring.

6. Confirm payment before the handover

Choose a payment method, confirm the timing and keep the purchase record. Do not assume a preliminary estimate has become an accepted transaction. Our Los Angeles Rolex buyer page explains how to start the local evaluation.

For an in-person purchase evaluation, contact Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014, or call 310-663-1340. Payment for agreed purchases is available by cash, bank wire or business check; confirm the arrangements before accepting.

Plan your evaluation in Downtown Los Angeles

Bring your items and any reports, receipts, or service records you already have. Contact us to discuss selling a luxury watch in Los Angeles and arrange an evaluation.

Call 310-663-1340 ↗

First establish why a value is needed and who will use it. An estate or insurance appraisal and a current purchase offer may use different dates and purposes. Keep the records, clarify authority to sell and request the appropriate service.

In this guide

  • Identify the person requesting a value
  • Organize the inheritance records and actual items
  • Keep tax records instead of assuming the proceeds are exempt
  • Compare a sale offer on its own terms
  • Discuss the collection in downtown Los Angeles

Identify the person requesting a value

An insurer, estate representative, family member and prospective buyer may need different information. Write down who requested a valuation, its purpose and any deadline. If a formal report is required, obtain the recipient’s requirements before booking an appraisal.

The Appraisal Foundation’s jewelry guide explains the importance of the intended use, value definition and effective date. A current offer to buy does not automatically meet a separate documentation requirement for an earlier date or another purpose.

Organize the inheritance records and actual items

Keep the estate inventory and any prior appraisal associated with the correct piece. Add photographs, receipts, laboratory reports and repair records when available. Use the estate jewelry inventory guide to label unknown details without guessing.

For watches, preserve matching boxes, papers, spare bracelet links and service documents. For jewelry, keep paired pieces and detached components together. Family recollections can help guide questions, but distinguish them from documented facts about age, maker or ownership.

Your immediate needUseful next step
Required estate documentationObtain the required date, purpose and report specifications
Insurance informationAsk the insurer what documentation it accepts
Considering a saleRequest a current purchase evaluation for identified items
Uncertain ownership or family agreementResolve the authority and items available for sale first

Keep tax records instead of assuming the proceeds are exempt

The IRS explains that selling inherited property can produce a taxable gain and that the property’s basis matters. Do not assume that receiving an inheritance makes a later jewelry sale automatically tax-free.

Keep the relevant estate valuation records and final sale receipt. A qualified tax professional can determine how the rules apply to your circumstances; an offer from a jewelry buyer does not resolve your reporting obligations.

Compare a sale offer on its own terms

Ask which pieces are included, whether further examination is required and what amount you would receive after stated deductions. Avoid using a universal fraction of an insurance appraisal as the standard for accepting or rejecting an offer.

If you want to keep selected items, have the offer for the remaining pieces clarified. The inherited jewelry decision guide helps you prepare for an evaluation while retaining control over that choice.

Discuss the collection in downtown Los Angeles

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds evaluates estate and inherited jewelry at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014. Contact us at 310-663-1340 with the items and documentation you have.

Our diamond buying covers natural cut and polished diamonds in any size or shape, excluding laboratory-grown, uncut and rough diamonds. Payment options for accepted purchases include cash, bank wire and business check; confirm the method and timing before finalizing.

Is an insurance appraisal always twice a resale offer?

No. There is no universal conversion ratio. Read the appraisal’s purpose, assumptions and date, and compare a separate purchase offer for the actual items.

Should I obtain an appraisal before speaking with a buyer?

Clarify whether you need a formal document or simply an offer to purchase. If an estate or insurer requires a report, confirm its requirements independently of the selling process.

Bring your items and any reports, receipts, or service records you already have. Contact us to discuss selling estate jewelry in Los Angeles and arrange an evaluation.

html:
There is no universal payout percentage for gold jewelry. A retail receipt, replacement appraisal, contained-gold estimate and current purchase offer answer different questions. Start with verified material and weight, then ask how the complete item and transaction terms affect the offer.

In this guide

  • A receipt records what was bought then
  • A metal estimate needs verified inputs
  • The complete item can need a different evaluation
  • A fixed percentage cannot define every reasonable offer
  • Bring the actual material, including uncertain pieces
  • Discuss your purchase offer in Downtown Los Angeles

A receipt records what was bought then

A retail price can include design, manufacture, distribution and the terms of that original sale. It is not a promise that a buyer will later purchase the piece for the same amount or a standard fraction of it.

Bring the receipt if it helps identify the item, maker or specifications. Use it as supporting information rather than treating the original total as today's minimum purchase amount.

A metal estimate needs verified inputs

Nominal 14K is 14 parts gold out of 24, and 18K is 18 out of 24. The World Gold Council's fineness guide explains those proportions. For equal net alloy weights, the higher fraction contains more gold; for different weights, both inputs are needed.

A dated fine-gold reference price can inform a theoretical material amount. Apply it to contained gold, not automatically to the gross weight of jewelry with stones or other components. Our valuation checklist identifies the inputs to verify.

The complete item can need a different evaluation

A broken chain still contains its remaining gold. A signed estate jewel, diamond Cuban bracelet or collectible watch may also have characteristics relevant to resale as an intact piece. Ask about those before treating the whole collection as scrap.

Do not add an intact-jewelry estimate to the full value of the same materials already inside it. Read our inherited-jewelry guide for keeping significant items identifiable during a collection evaluation.

A fixed percentage cannot define every reasonable offer

Material form, verified information, resale potential, business costs and transaction terms can differ. An article cannot establish a minimum or maximum fair percentage for every buyer and piece. A higher or lower number needs context before it can be assessed.

Ask whether the amount is final, which pieces it covers and whether charges or further checks remain. If one quote excludes a diamond while another includes it, resolve that difference before comparing totals. The offer checklist provides a consistent record.

Bring the actual material, including uncertain pieces

A stamp can guide examination but does not establish authenticity by itself. The FTC explains gold alloy, filled and plated descriptions. A plated item's entire weight should not be valued as though it were a solid gold alloy.

html:
Use this checklist to prepare your gold, compare purchase offers, and confirm payment terms before choosing where to sell in Los Angeles.

In this guide

  • Where Can You Sell Gold in Los Angeles?
  • How Is the Value of Your Gold Calculated?
  • Does a Gold Buyer Pay the Full Spot Price?
  • How Can You Get the Best Price When Selling Gold in Los Angeles?
  • What Types of Gold Can You Sell?
  • Should You Sell Broken Gold Jewelry?
  • What About Designer or Estate Jewelry?
  • What Should You Bring When Selling Gold?
  • Questions to Ask a Gold Buyer Before Selling
  • Red Flags When Choosing a Gold Buyer
  • Is It Better to Sell Gold Locally in Los Angeles?
  • Where Can I Sell Gold Near Me in Los Angeles?
  • Frequently Asked Questions About Selling Gold in Los Angeles
  • Get Your Gold Evaluated in Los Angeles

If you’re wondering where to sell gold in Los Angeles, the best place is not necessarily the buyer advertising the biggest number. The better choice is a reputable gold buyer who clearly explains how your gold is tested, weighed, and valued before you decide whether to sell.

Los Angeles has many options for selling gold, including pawn shops, jewelry stores, precious-metal dealers, and dedicated gold buyers. Understanding how these businesses calculate an offer can help you compare buyers and make a more informed decision.

At Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds, we believe sellers should understand what affects the value of their gold before accepting an offer.

Where Can You Sell Gold in Los Angeles?

Los Angeles sellers generally have several options.

Professional Gold Buyers

A professional gold buyer specializes in evaluating precious metals and may purchase gold jewelry, broken jewelry, coins, bullion, dental gold, and other gold items.

A knowledgeable buyer should be able to explain the testing and valuation process so you understand how the offer was determined.

Pawn Shops

Pawn shops commonly purchase gold and may be convenient when someone wants to sell an item quickly.

However, offers can vary significantly from one shop to another. A pawn shop also operates a broader business involving many types of merchandise, whereas a precious-metals buyer may have more specialized experience evaluating gold.

If you’re considering this option, see our guide on How Much Do Pawn Shops Pay for Gold? What Los Angeles Sellers Should Know.

Jewelry Stores

Some jewelry stores purchase used gold jewelry, although buying gold from the public may not be their primary business.

This can be an option for certain pieces, but sellers should ask whether the item is being valued primarily for its gold content, its resale potential, or both.

Online Gold Buyers

Online buyers allow sellers to mail their gold for evaluation.

This can be convenient, but it means temporarily giving up possession of your jewelry before receiving an offer. Before mailing valuable items, carefully review the company’s shipping procedures, insurance coverage, return policy, reputation, and payment terms.

How Is the Value of Your Gold Calculated?

Several factors determine what your gold may be worth.

Gold Purity

Gold jewelry is commonly marked according to karat purity.

Examples include:

  • 10K gold
  • 14K gold
  • 18K gold
  • 22K gold
  • 24K gold

Pure gold is 24 karat. Lower-karat jewelry contains gold mixed with other metals.

For example, 14K gold contains a smaller percentage of pure gold than 18K gold. Because of that difference, two pieces with the same weight can have different underlying gold values.

The Federal Trade Commission explains common gold, plated and filled jewelry descriptions. Use the description as a starting point and have the actual material evaluated.

Weight

After determining purity, the weight of the gold becomes another major factor.

Professional buyers generally weigh gold using a calibrated scale. Stones, non-gold components, and other materials may need to be considered separately when determining the amount of actual gold in an item.

Current Gold Market Price

Gold is traded internationally, and its market price changes over time.

The current gold price provides an important reference point when determining the underlying metal value of an item. The World Gold Council publishes dated gold-price information. Check the date, currency and unit before using a quote as a reference.

However, the market price of pure gold should not be confused with the amount a buyer will necessarily offer for jewelry. Buyers must consider purity, refining or resale costs, operating expenses, and other factors.

Does a Gold Buyer Pay the Full Spot Price?

Usually, you should not expect a buyer to simply multiply the item’s total weight by the quoted price of pure gold.

The advertised spot price generally refers to pure gold in the wholesale market. Most jewelry is not 24K pure gold.

For example, a 14K necklace contains gold as well as other metals. Its theoretical precious-metal value therefore differs from the value of the same weight in pure 24K gold.

A buyer’s actual offer can also reflect testing, processing, refining, resale potential, and the buyer’s operating margin.

This is why comparing offers based only on a percentage advertised in an ad can be misleading.

How Can You Get the Best Price When Selling Gold in Los Angeles?

You don’t need to be a precious-metals expert to make a better-informed decision.

Know What You Have

Before visiting a buyer, look for karat markings such as 10K, 14K, 18K, 22K, or 24K.

Keep in mind that a stamp is useful information but may still need to be professionally verified.

Separate Different Karats

If you have several pieces, consider separating them according to their marked purity before the evaluation.

Different karats should generally not be treated as though they contain the same amount of gold.

Ask to See the Weight

A transparent evaluation should allow you to understand the weight being used to calculate your offer.

Ask what unit of measurement is being used and whether stones or non-gold components affect the calculation.

Ask How Purity Is Tested

Gold can be evaluated using several methods depending on the item and buyer.

Ask the buyer how they determine purity and whether the testing can be explained to you during the evaluation.

Compare More Than One Offer

If you are uncertain about an offer, you can obtain another evaluation before selling.

Gold jewelry is valuable property. You should feel comfortable understanding the offer before making your decision.

What Types of Gold Can You Sell?

Depending on the buyer, you may be able to sell:

  • Gold necklaces
  • Gold bracelets
  • Gold rings
  • Gold earrings
  • Broken gold jewelry
  • Unwanted jewelry
  • Scrap gold
  • Gold coins
  • Gold bullion
  • Gold watches
  • Dental gold
  • Estate jewelry

Don’t assume an item has no value simply because it is broken, outdated, tangled, or missing stones. Its precious-metal content may still have value.

Should You Sell Broken Gold Jewelry?

Broken gold can still have significant value because the underlying gold does not cease to be valuable simply because the jewelry can no longer be worn.

Broken chains, single earrings, damaged bracelets, bent rings, and other unwanted pieces can potentially be evaluated according to their precious-metal content.

Before throwing damaged jewelry away, consider having it evaluated.

What About Designer or Estate Jewelry?

Not every piece should automatically be treated as scrap gold.

Certain designer jewelry, antique pieces, estate jewelry, watches, gemstones, and collectible items may have value beyond their precious-metal content.

A knowledgeable buyer should recognize when an item deserves additional evaluation rather than automatically treating everything as scrap.

This is particularly important when selling inherited jewelry or an estate collection when you may not know the history or significance of individual pieces.

What Should You Bring When Selling Gold?

Bring the gold items you want evaluated along with any documentation you have that may be relevant.

For certain jewelry, watches, coins, or collectible pieces, useful documentation can include original receipts, boxes, certificates, grading reports, or previous appraisals.

Documentation isn’t always necessary to evaluate ordinary gold jewelry, but it can be useful for pieces whose value may extend beyond their metal content.

Also bring valid identification if required for the transaction.

Questions to Ask a Gold Buyer Before Selling

Before accepting an offer, consider asking:

How did you determine the purity?

The buyer should be able to explain how the gold was tested.

What weight are you using?

Make sure you understand the weight used in the calculation.

What gold price are you referencing?

Because the market changes, ask what reference price is being used at the time of your evaluation.

Are gemstones or collectible value included?

If your jewelry contains diamonds, gemstones, or has potential designer or collectible value, ask whether those factors were considered separately.

Is the evaluation free?

Ask whether there is any obligation or fee before agreeing to an evaluation.

Red Flags When Choosing a Gold Buyer

Be cautious when a buyer:

  • Refuses to explain how an offer was calculated
  • Will not let you see or understand the weighing process
  • Pressures you to sell immediately
  • Makes claims that sound unrealistic
  • Provides unclear information about the business
  • Cannot explain how purity was determined

A legitimate transaction should give you enough information to make your own decision.

Is It Better to Sell Gold Locally in Los Angeles?

For many sellers, working with a local buyer has an important advantage: you can have the item evaluated while you are present.

You can ask questions, understand the testing process, receive an offer, and decide whether you want to proceed without mailing your valuables away.

Los Angeles also has a large jewelry and precious-metals market, giving sellers multiple options when comparing evaluations.

Where Can I Sell Gold Near Me in Los Angeles?

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds is at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014. We buy scrap gold, Cuban chains and bracelets with or without diamonds, gold jewelry, gold coins and silver coins. Single pieces and large quantities are welcome.

Arrange your visit or call 310-663-1340. Describe a substantial collection in advance and discuss payment by cash, bank wire or business check. Our first-evaluation guide explains what to expect during the visit.

Frequently Asked Questions About Selling Gold in Los Angeles

Where is the best place to sell gold in Los Angeles?

The best choice depends on what you’re selling. Look for an established buyer who specializes in the type of item you have, clearly explains the evaluation, and allows you to understand the offer before making a decision.

How much is my gold worth today?

Your gold’s value depends on its purity, weight, the current gold market price, and potentially its condition, brand, gemstones, or collectible value. Because gold prices change, an in-person evaluation provides a more current estimate.

Is 14K gold worth selling?

Yes. Although 14K gold is not pure gold, it contains a substantial amount of gold and can have meaningful value depending on its weight and current market conditions.

Can I sell gold without a receipt?

Ordinary gold jewelry can often be evaluated without its original purchase receipt, although identification or other documentation may be required for the transaction. Special pieces may benefit from certificates, grading reports, receipts, or other provenance documentation.

Should I clean my gold before selling it?

Usually, extensive cleaning is unnecessary when an item is primarily being evaluated for its precious-metal content. Avoid aggressive cleaning methods that could damage gemstones, finishes, antique pieces, or collectible jewelry.

Can I sell broken gold?

Yes. Broken gold jewelry can still have value because its precious-metal content remains valuable even when the item is no longer wearable.

Get Your Gold Evaluated in Los Angeles

Selling gold should not require guessing what your jewelry is worth.

Understanding purity, weight, current gold prices, and the type of item you’re selling can help you evaluate an offer more confidently.

If you have gold jewelry, broken gold, coins, bullion, estate jewelry, or other valuables you’d like evaluated, Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds can provide an in-person evaluation in Los Angeles.

Bring your items in, learn how they’re evaluated, and decide whether the offer is right for you.

Plan your evaluation in Downtown Los Angeles

We buy scrap gold, Cuban chains and bracelets with or without diamonds, gold coins, and silver coins. Single pieces and large quantities are welcome. Payment is available by cash, bank wire, or business check.

Gold buying in Downtown Los Angeles · 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014

Call 310-663-1340 ↗

  • World Gold Council: gold alloys, color and purity

Separate learning about your jewelry from agreeing to sell it. Decide which pieces you are willing to consider, ask about any service terms in advance, and confirm the exact items and amount before accepting a purchase offer.

In this guide

  • Decide what you are comfortable considering
  • Clarify the appointment and service terms
  • Bring an organized collection
  • Ask for an offer you can understand
  • Take the next step that fits your purpose

Decide what you are comfortable considering

You do not need to make one decision about an entire inheritance. Set aside pieces you want to keep, identify those you are comfortable discussing and leave uncertain items in a separate group. A photograph or written family history may also be worth preserving independently of a sale.

People attach different meanings to inherited jewelry. Keeping a piece, selling it or waiting can each be a reasonable personal choice. If other people share ownership or decision-making responsibility, resolve that before committing items to a transaction.

Clarify the appointment and service terms

Describe the collection when contacting a buyer. Ask what to bring, how the appointment works and whether any proposed service has a charge. A no-obligation purchase discussion should leave the sale decision with you, but it should not be confused with an agreement for separate paid work.

The Appraisal Foundation’s guide distinguishes the scope and intended use of a formal appraisal. If your purpose is insurance or estate documentation, establish that requirement rather than assuming a buyer’s offer supplies the document you need.

Bring an organized collection

Keep matching jewelry and any detached components together. Bring existing receipts, reports and repair history, and tell the evaluator which items you are considering for sale. Label information you do not know as unknown.

If your collection includes a Rolex, the local watch-buyer guide helps you compare evaluation arrangements. For diamond pieces, the diamond identification and selling guide explains what to establish before discussing value.

GIA’s estate jewelry guidance highlights condition and repairs as useful details to examine. Our inventory guide provides a simple way to record those observations without trying to price every piece yourself.

Ask for an offer you can understand

Before decidingClarify
Included jewelryThe exact pieces covered by the amount
Partial saleWhether keeping selected items changes the remaining offer
Further examinationAny conditions that could change the number
Time to considerHow long the offer remains available
PaymentThe final amount, method and expected availability

If something is unclear, ask for an explanation before accepting. Keep a written summary when comparing offers. A decision to wait does not require a buyer to keep a price available indefinitely, so record the offer’s actual terms.

Take the next step that fits your purpose

You may request a purchase evaluation now, seek required appraisal documentation or wait while you discuss the collection with family. The inherited jewelry valuation guide explains how those purposes differ.

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds offers an estate jewelry buying service at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014. Contact us at 310-663-1340 to describe your collection. Our diamond buying is for natural cut and polished diamonds in any size or shape; we do not buy laboratory-grown, uncut or rough diamonds.

Can I decide to keep a piece after hearing an offer?

Make your decision before accepting the transaction. If you remove an item from a proposed collection sale, ask for the revised scope and amount.

Does no obligation to sell mean every appraisal service is free?

No. A purchase discussion and a separately commissioned appraisal are different services. Confirm any proposed charges and deliverables before authorizing work.

Plan your evaluation in Downtown Los Angeles

Bring your items and any reports, receipts, or service records you already have. Contact us to discuss selling estate jewelry in Los Angeles and arrange an evaluation.

Selling estate jewelry in Los Angeles · 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014

Call 310-663-1340 ↗

To prepare natural diamonds for sale, keep the jewelry intact, match each report to its item, separate pieces you want to keep and note known condition details. Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds buys natural polished diamonds of any size and shape in Downtown Los Angeles.

In this guide

  • Start with the items you want to sell
  • Keep complete jewelry and matching components together
  • Match each document to the correct diamond
  • Separate identification, quality and money
  • Make the evaluation conversation specific
  • Plan your Downtown Los Angeles visit

Start with the items you want to sell

Place the pieces you may sell separately from anything you intend to keep. For a collection, make a short item list: a loose oval diamond, a solitaire ring, a pair of earrings or an eternity band. Use descriptions you know rather than estimated grades.

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds buys natural, cut and polished diamonds only. Any size and any shape are welcome, whether loose or set in jewelry. We do not buy laboratory-grown diamonds, rough material or uncut crystals. Our large-diamond guide covers substantial individual stones and multi-stone jewelry.

Keep complete jewelry and matching components together

Bring matching earrings, necklace components, removed bracelet links and accessories you already have. Note missing parts. An offer for a complete design may cover more than the single stone you first intended to discuss.

Leave stones in their settings until you have discussed any proposed work. If a stone is loose or a clasp is damaged, keep the item in its own suitable container and point out the condition. Do not undertake polishing, repairs or stone removal solely to prepare for an initial conversation.

Match each document to the correct diamond

Gather grading reports, receipts and repair records. Put a copy of the relevant document with each item on your list. A box or a familiar-looking certificate is useful context, but the actual document still needs to be matched to the piece.

For a GIA report, Report Check provides a way to consult the available record. If you have no report, tell us what you know and leave uncertain details open. Ask what additional examination would be useful before paying for it.

Separate identification, quality and money

First establish what the stone is. GIA explains the specialist identification of natural and laboratory-grown diamonds. Appearance alone is not a reliable origin test.

Next, consider the stone's quality information. The 4Cs help describe diamonds, while the condition of the actual item and the details of its setting still matter. Keep an individual diamond's weight separate from the total weight in an entire bracelet or ring.

Finally, discuss a purchase amount for the item. An appraisal and a grading report have different purposes. Neither a prior insurance amount nor an advertised retail price guarantees a current offer.

Make the evaluation conversation specific

Explain whether you are considering the whole collection or selected pieces. Ask which items a proposal includes and what information remains uncertain. If further testing or alteration is suggested, discuss its purpose and arrangements before agreeing.

  • Does the offer include the mounting and all accent stones?
  • Are the report and stone matched, or is further identification needed?
  • Are any checks, costs or conditions outstanding?
  • What happens to the amount if you retain one item?
  • Which payment method and timing are agreed?

Use the same item list when comparing offers. Our offer comparison guide explains how to keep those proposals comparable.

Plan your Downtown Los Angeles visit

Call 310-663-1340 or contact us with the number and type of items you have. Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds is at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014. Confirm the visit arrangements and bring your organized pieces and records.

Cash, bank wire and business-check payment are available for agreed purchases. Review the final offer and decide which items you wish to sell. There is no need to turn uncertainty about a family piece into a guess about its grade or origin.

Do you consider small natural diamonds as well as large ones?

Yes. Our natural polished diamond buying covers any size and shape, including diamonds in complete jewelry.

What if I am unsure whether my diamond is natural?

Share any existing identification report and explain the uncertainty when you contact us. We do not buy laboratory-grown or uncut diamonds.

Plan your evaluation in Downtown Los Angeles

Bring your items and any reports, receipts, or service records you already have. Contact us to discuss selling diamonds in Los Angeles and arrange an evaluation.

Call 310-663-1340 ↗

A gold Rolex Day-Date purchase offer depends on the exact reference, configuration, condition and included components. Bring the watch, bracelet links and existing records; a gold-price chart or generic online range cannot price the complete timepiece.

In this guide

  • Identify the Day-Date you actually have
  • Include the bracelet in the evaluation
  • Separate configuration from later changes
  • Use service history and condition together
  • Compare an offer without assuming an investment return
  • Arrange an individual Day-Date evaluation

Identify the Day-Date you actually have

Record the reference from available documents and describe the dial, bezel, case and bracelet. Avoid choosing a reference solely because a current online image looks similar. Earlier examples and later modifications may need additional research.

The official Rolex Day-Date collection describes the model family and its precious-metal configurations. The President bracelet is closely associated with this collection, but a nickname is not a complete description of an individual watch.

Include the bracelet in the evaluation

Bring detached links and note any replacement clasp or bracelet work you know about. Ask how length, wear, repairs and the relationship of the bracelet to the case are being considered.

A full-watch weight includes non-gold components. Do not multiply that weight by a pure-gold price or assume every fitted component matches the case material. The gold Rolex selling guide discusses complete-watch assessment.

Separate configuration from later changes

Disclose dial, bezel or diamond-setting changes if known. Ask the evaluator to distinguish original components, manufacturer service replacements and aftermarket alterations. The presence of gemstones does not by itself establish factory setting or their natural origin.

Do not open the case yourself to check a movement. A familiar logo, serial number or substantial feel cannot authenticate the complete watch. Our Rolex authentication guide explains the limits of visual shortcuts.

Use service history and condition together

Bring service invoices, including any description of parts replaced. A prior service date does not guarantee present operation or water resistance. Describe current problems honestly.

Before arranging polishing or repair solely for a sale, discuss an evaluation in the watch's present condition. Rolex's care and service information is the primary source for manufacturer support.

Compare an offer without assuming an investment return

A luxury watch can rise or fall in resale value. Neither its precious-metal content nor brand name creates a guaranteed resale floor for the amount you paid. Gold price changes also do not translate into a fixed percentage change in a complete Day-Date offer.

Compare the same reference, condition, accessories and sale terms. An advertised watch with a warranty or Rolex Certified Pre-Owned programme coverage is not equivalent to every privately presented example.

Arrange an individual Day-Date evaluation

Review the gold Rolex comparison checklist, then bring the actual watch and available records.

Our step-by-step Rolex selling guide also covers agreeing on the examination, documenting the offer and confirming payment before handover.

For an in-person purchase evaluation, contact Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014, or call 310-663-1340. Payment for agreed purchases is available by cash, bank wire or business check; confirm the arrangements before accepting.

Plan your evaluation in Downtown Los Angeles

Bring your items and any reports, receipts, or service records you already have. Contact us to discuss selling a luxury watch in Los Angeles and arrange an evaluation.

To compare gold offers in Los Angeles, request an outright purchase offer for the same items from each buyer. Record the tested purity, metal weight, treatment of diamonds, final amount and payment terms; a pawn loan is a different transaction.

In this guide

  • Ask for a purchase offer for your gold
  • Prepare one consistent collection for each evaluation
  • Compare the details behind each number
  • Bring scrap gold, Cuban links or a larger collection

Ask for a purchase offer for your gold

A pawn shop may buy an item outright or lend money against it. Start by saying which transaction you want. The CFPB’s financial-products guide explains that a pawn loan uses an item as collateral. A loan amount and a purchase offer therefore answer different questions.

If your goal is to sell, record the amount you would receive for transferring ownership of the listed items. Do not compare that figure with a loan advance, an insurance appraisal or an online advertisement for a different piece.

Prepare one consistent collection for each evaluation

Photograph your pieces and make a simple inventory before visiting buyers. Separate chains, bracelets, rings, coins and loose items into identifiable groups. Note broken clasps, missing stones and any marks you can read; leave uncertain details marked unknown.

The FTC’s jewelry guide explains distinctions among gold alloys and gold coatings. A gold-colored bracelet is not automatically solid gold. Bring the actual item so its material and construction can be assessed.

Keep diamond-set Cuban chains and designer or antique jewelry intact. Ask for the whole piece to be considered before discussing scrap value. For coins, keep any existing holders and identifying paperwork with the corresponding coin.

Compare the details behind each number

RecordQuestion to ask
Items includedDoes this amount cover every listed piece?
Weight and purityWhat metal weight and karat were used?
Diamonds and workmanshipHow were stones and the complete design considered?
Final amountAre there any deductions from this figure?
Payment and timingHow and when will I receive the agreed amount?

Request offers close enough together that you can discuss any change in the underlying market reference. A telephone estimate may depend on details that examination later changes. Our gold-offer calculation guide explains why a percentage alone cannot establish which offer is stronger.

Bring scrap gold, Cuban links or a larger collection

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds buys gold jewelry, scrap gold, Cuban chains and bracelets with or without diamonds, gold coins and silver coins. Single pieces and large quantities are welcome. Our Downtown Los Angeles gold-buying service can evaluate the items you are considering selling.

We buy natural cut and polished diamonds in any size or shape. Other gemstone buying is limited to large, high-quality stones, including green Colombian emeralds, Burmese rubies and Ceylon blue sapphires. Certificates are optional.

Visit 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014, or contact us at 310-663-1340 to discuss your collection. Payment options are cash, bank wire or business check. Confirm the final amount and timing before accepting.

Does a gold buyer always pay more than a pawn shop?

No universal rule establishes that. Compare actual purchase offers for the same items and terms.

Can I compare offers without removing the diamonds?

Bring the jewelry intact. Ask what can be assessed while mounted and how any estimates affect the offer before authorizing further work.

To sell Tiffany jewelry in Los Angeles, bring the complete piece and any matching purchase records, diamond certificate, box or repair documents you already have. The buyer should examine the jewelry itself and explain the final purchase offer.

In this guide

  • Identify the actual Tiffany piece
  • Match each document to the jewelry
  • Describe condition before arranging repairs
  • Compare a purchase offer with the right reference
  • Arrange a Downtown Los Angeles evaluation

Identify the actual Tiffany piece

Start with what you know: jewelry type, collection name, metal, ring size or chain length, and any stones. If the piece was inherited or received as a gift, say which details come from records and which come from memory. You do not need to guess a model or manufacturing year.

Bring the complete necklace, bracelet, ring or pair of earrings. Include detached components, matching backs or other original parts you still have. A photograph of a similar retail item can help explain a design, but it does not establish the identity or current condition of your piece.

Match each document to the jewelry

Tiffany describes its Diamond Certificate as documenting the identity and grades of the relevant Tiffany diamond. It is useful information to bring with the matching piece. Do not assume a document for one diamond describes every stone in a jewelry collection.

What you haveHow to organize it
Receipt or purchase recordKeep it with the item it describes
Diamond certificateBring the complete document and matching jewelry
Repair or resizing recordNote the date and work performed
Box and accessoriesInclude existing items without buying replacements for the visit

If documents are missing, tell the buyer before the evaluation. Papers and packaging can provide context, but the actual item still needs examination. Neither a branded box nor a copied document establishes authenticity by itself.

Describe condition before arranging repairs

List known resizing, engraving, replacement stones, broken links or missing components. Avoid presenting a repaired piece as untouched. Keep earlier service records even when the work was performed by a different jeweler.

html:
14 karat gold is nominally 14 parts gold out of 24, approximately 58.33%. A 585 mark expresses a related fineness convention. Neither a mark nor the color alone verifies the material, construction, condition or purchase value of a particular piece.

In this guide

  • Read karat as a fraction, not a weight
  • Know what a 585 mark is claiming
  • Color and purity describe different characteristics
  • Distinguish hollow construction from plated material
  • Inspect the actual design and condition
  • Have your 14K jewelry evaluated

Read karat as a fraction, not a weight

14K does not mean a ring contains 14 grams of gold. It describes the nominal proportion in the alloy. The World Gold Council's purity table connects karat descriptions with common fineness markings.

At nominal 14/24 purity, 12 grams of verified alloy contains seven grams of gold. That calculation assumes the 12 grams is the applicable alloy weight, excluding stones and other components.

Know what a 585 mark is claiming

585 expresses 585 parts gold per thousand, or 58.5%. Nominal 14/24 arithmetic gives about 58.33%; avoid silently treating different rounded inputs as exact measurements. The actual item still needs evaluation.

Look near a clasp or inside a band for clues, but do not conclude that an unmarked piece is worthless or a marked one is authentic. Repairs, mixed components and surface layers can require closer inspection.

Color and purity describe different characteristics

Yellow, white and rose gold can all be made at 14K. The other metals and any surface finish affect appearance. A pale color is not proof that a ring is platinum, and a warm color is not proof of a higher karat.

See our white and yellow gold comparison for finish and resale questions. If a particular alloy ingredient matters to you, ask the maker rather than inferring the full composition from the karat.

Distinguish hollow construction from plated material

A hollow chain can be made of a genuine gold alloy while weighing less than a similar-looking solid chain. A gold-plated piece has a surface layer over another material. These are different descriptions, as the FTC's jewelry guide explains.

Heft and magnetic response are not sufficient to identify an entire item. Have uncertain pieces assessed instead of relying on a home test. Our testing guide covers what measurements can establish.

Inspect the actual design and condition

A 14K label does not guarantee secure prongs, an unworn band or suitability for every activity. Construction, alloy, thickness, use and prior repairs all matter. Keep care questions specific to the maker, finish and any stones in the piece.

For a substantial necklace, the 14K chain guide covers links and clasps. For a value estimate, use our 14K per-gram guide and check the current reference rather than an undated article price.

Have your 14K jewelry evaluated

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds buys 14K jewelry, scrap and Cuban chains, with or without diamonds. Large collections are welcome. Arrange an evaluation in Downtown Los Angeles and discuss cash, bank wire or business-check payment.

We buy scrap gold, Cuban chains and bracelets with or without diamonds, gold coins, and silver coins. Single pieces and large quantities are welcome. Payment is available by cash, bank wire, or business check.

Start with model and material details

A Cartier LOVE bracelet, Juste un Clou design, ring or necklace should be evaluated as the particular item in front of the buyer. Record the collection or reference if known, size, visible markings and accompanying paperwork. Leave uncertain details open for examination.

Check the materials and stone arrangement for the exact item. A complete piece may include non-gold components, so its entire scale weight is not automatically pure-gold weight. Match available descriptions to the actual jewelry rather than assuming that a similar-looking piece has the same construction.

Keep the jewelry and its components together

Bring original components and accessories you already own, along with purchase, sizing and repair records. Note missing screws, damaged clasps, replaced stones, alterations or engraving. Do not force a closure or dismantle a bracelet to prepare it for inspection.

For a Cartier watch, also describe its operation and bring service records and spare bracelet links. Tell the buyer that you have a timepiece so its movement, reference and components can be considered alongside its materials.

Separate records from authentication conclusions

A hallmark, serial number, box or photograph is one piece of information. The buyer still needs to examine the jewelry and consider whether the records correspond to it. If you inherited the piece, explain what is documented and what was passed down verbally.

Cartier’s official FAQ states limits on information and authentication for items acquired outside its boutiques or authorized retailers. Do not assume a third-party purchase automatically qualifies for a brand authentication service. Ask Cartier directly about any brand service you are considering.

Ask whether the proposed amount covers the complete jewelry and all included components. Original retail prices and insurance values are not promises of resale proceeds; GIA’s appraisal guidance explains the importance of valuation purpose.

Compare offers for the same item in the same condition. Record any deductions, payment method and timing. The Los Angeles jewelry-selling guide helps compare transaction options without assuming every buyer offers the same terms.

Our separate gemstone buying is limited to large, high-quality stones, including green Colombian emeralds, Burmese rubies and Ceylon blue sapphires. Certificates are optional. Natural cut and polished diamonds are welcome in any size or shape.

Must I repair Cartier jewelry before asking for an offer?

No. Discuss it in its current condition before paying for work that may not be recovered through a sale.

Do boxes and papers guarantee a higher amount?

No. Bring them if available, but the actual item and the complete evaluation determine the offer.

html:
Compare the actual alloy, finish and ring construction. White gold is a gold alloy that is often rhodium plated; platinum jewelry uses platinum alloys. Neither the metal name nor a generic price comparison establishes the upkeep or resale of a particular piece.

In this guide

  • Read the full metal description
  • Compare the questions that affect ownership
  • Avoid universal durability and maintenance promises
  • Compare full quotes instead of permanent price rankings
  • Evaluate an existing piece for resale

Read the full metal description

Platinum and white gold can look similar, but they are different material descriptions. The FTC’s precious-metal jewelry guide explains how purity is expressed. A 950 platinum description refers to 95 percent platinum, while 18K gold describes 75 percent gold in the alloy.

The World Gold Council explains white gold as gold alloyed with white metals, usually with a rhodium finish. The alloy and the coating should be considered separately. Ask what the piece is made from and which surface treatment, if any, is present.

Compare the questions that affect ownership

QuestionPlatinumWhite gold
What is the alloy?Ask for platinum fineness and alloy detailsAsk for gold karat and alloy details
What finish is present?Identify polish, texture or any applied coatingEstablish whether there is rhodium plating
What work is likely?Discuss condition, sizing and setting repairsDiscuss those repairs and any finish maintenance
What is the full cost?Obtain an item-specific quoteObtain an equivalent quote for comparison

Try the actual rings if buying. Compare fit, band dimensions and the height of the setting. A similar outline does not mean that two rings have the same metal weight, workmanship or comfort.

Avoid universal durability and maintenance promises

GIA’s platinum-alloy guidance explains that different alloys have different working properties and that compatible materials matter for repairs. That is a reason to ask about the specific ring, rather than assuming every platinum piece behaves identically.

GIA’s ring-material guide discusses platinum patina and notes that some manufacturers rhodium plate platinum too. Platinum should therefore not be described as universally maintenance-free or never coated.

For either metal, ask how the finish and stone setting should be inspected and maintained. Wear patterns, construction and previous work affect the discussion. Obtain advice for the particular item instead of assuming that all white gold needs replating on a fixed calendar.

Compare full quotes instead of permanent price rankings

A finished ring price includes more than its metal. Design, workmanship, stones, brand and seller terms affect the quote. If you want a meaningful comparison, request the same stone and comparable dimensions in the two metals, then identify any differences in what is included.

Ask for current sizing, repair and refinishing estimates where relevant. Record whether a service is included or charged separately. Avoid a long-term cost calculation built from invented maintenance intervals and assumed prices.

Evaluate an existing piece for resale

A resale discussion needs the actual composition, relevant metal weight and condition. Any diamonds or other stones must be distinguished from metal-content arithmetic. Ask whether the offer covers the complete piece and how its design or supported maker attribution was considered.

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds is at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014. Contact us at 310-663-1340 to describe your precious-metal jewelry and arrange an evaluation. For gold pieces, review our gold jewelry buying service and the white gold diamond ring guide.

Is platinum always worth more than white gold?

No fixed ranking establishes an offer for finished jewelry. Compare the identified metal content, complete item and actual transaction terms using current information.

Can I identify either metal from color alone?

No. Similar surface appearances can hide different alloys or finishes. Records and examination are needed to establish what the piece contains.

We buy scrap gold, Cuban chains and bracelets with or without diamonds, gold coins, and silver coins. Single pieces and large quantities are welcome. Payment is available by cash, bank wire, or business check.

Start by establishing what the stone is and what information is available about it. Then consider its quality, condition and complete setting before requesting an offer. A sparkle test, old receipt or generic online price cannot replace examination of your item.

In this guide

  • Identify what you have before estimating a price
  • Collect the quality information that is already available
  • Keep different documents in their proper roles
  • Present the complete piece or collection
  • Request an offer and decide what works for you

Identify what you have before estimating a price

GIA describes diamond as a material composed of carbon with a particular crystal structure. For an owner, the practical first question is whether an unfamiliar stone is a diamond and what is known about its origin and condition.

Describe the item as you know it: a ring, a loose stone, earrings or a necklace. If a family member called it a diamond but there is no supporting record, explain that uncertainty. A visual sparkle or fog test is not enough to establish identity, natural origin or value.

Collect the quality information that is already available

GIA’s four quality factors are cut, color, clarity and carat weight. Shape describes the outline, such as oval or round; cut quality concerns how the stone has been fashioned. Carat measures weight and should be read alongside the stone’s millimeter dimensions.

Do not assume every diamond should be described by the same color terminology. Our report and grading chart guide explains the context needed to read the fields. If no report is available, ask what can be established through examination instead of assigning grades yourself.

Keep different documents in their proper roles

RecordWhat it can help explain
Laboratory reportThe information recorded about the examined stone
Purchase receiptThe original transaction and item description
AppraisalA value assigned for its stated purpose and date
Repair recordKnown alterations, replaced parts or work performed
Current buyer’s offerThe proposed amount and purchase conditions

GIA explains the difference between grading and monetary appraisal. Keep the purpose of each document clear, and ask the evaluator to match the records to your actual item. A paper associated with a jewelry box may concern another piece.

Present the complete piece or collection

Bring jewelry intact, including matching earrings, detached parts and any original supporting documents. Keep loose stones individually contained. Note known chips, repairs and replacement stones without trying to repair or dismantle the item yourself.

If selling gold and diamonds together, ask how the relevant metal weight and the stones are considered. Do not count a complete ring’s weight as pure gold or add a separate metal estimate to an offer that already includes the setting. Keep any luxury watches or attributed designer pieces identifiable within a larger collection.

Request an offer and decide what works for you

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds buys natural cut and polished diamonds in any size or shape, along with gold jewelry and scrap gold. We do not buy laboratory-grown, uncut or rough diamonds.

We are at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014. Contact us at 310-663-1340, bring existing records and ask for the final amount, included items and payment terms. The diamond selling decision guide can help you consider an offer against your own priorities.

Does a grading report state what a buyer must pay?

No. The laboratory information and the purchase amount serve different roles. Ask for a separate offer for the actual item.

Can I bring a diamond item whose details are unknown?

Describe the uncertainty when contacting us and bring the records you have. An examination is the starting point for establishing whether it falls within our buying service.

Plan your evaluation in Downtown Los Angeles

Bring your items and any reports, receipts, or service records you already have. Contact us to discuss selling diamonds in Los Angeles and arrange an evaluation.

Selling diamonds in Los Angeles · 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014

Call 310-663-1340 ↗

Compare the type of transaction before comparing prices: an outright purchase, a consignment agreement and an auction estimate are different proposals. For each route, confirm the inspection process, net amount, custody and payment terms.

In this guide

  • Consider an in-person purchase
  • Check an online buyer's custody and return terms
  • Understand consignment and auction proposals
  • Verify manufacturer affiliation separately
  • Compare the same complete package
  • Arrange your Downtown Los Angeles evaluation

Consider an in-person purchase

A local buyer can inspect the watch while you discuss its condition and records. Ask whether the proposed figure is an outright purchase amount and whether any further inspection is required before it becomes final.

Call ahead with the reference if known, missing accessories and any damage. A physical location makes a visit possible; it does not itself prove the buyer's qualifications or guarantee the highest offer. Our Los Angeles Rolex buyer guide explains the local service.

Check an online buyer's custody and return terms

Before sending a watch, confirm who receives it, the documented shipping arrangements, coverage limits, the inspection process and what happens if you decline. Determine whether an online figure is only an estimate.

Ask who pays return expenses and how the watch's condition and accessories will be recorded. Compare the final purchase amount after any agreed costs, rather than assuming a remote buyer always pays more or less.

Understand consignment and auction proposals

A consignment listing asks another party to find a purchaser. An auction estimate concerns a possible future sale. Neither is automatically an immediate purchase offer for the quoted amount.

Read the agreement for commission, reserve or minimum terms, insurance, unsold-item costs, withdrawal conditions and payment after a completed sale. Request the actual terms instead of relying on generic industry percentages.

Verify manufacturer affiliation separately

Retailer status and a willingness to buy your particular watch are separate questions. Rolex explains its Certified Pre-Owned programme and participating Official Retailers. Check a claimed affiliation through the manufacturer and ask the business directly what buying services it offers.

An independent buyer's offer should not imply manufacturer certification. The buyer trust checklist helps assess clear descriptions and transaction records.

Compare the same complete package

List the watch, bracelet, links, box and papers included in each proposal. Note the evaluation date, final amount and any unresolved conditions. A warranty-backed retail asking price is not the same as your net selling proceeds.

Keep the watch in its current condition while comparing options. Refer to Rolex's care information for manufacturer support and avoid opening or polishing an unfamiliar watch yourself.

Arrange your Downtown Los Angeles evaluation

Use the Rolex selling checklist to prepare the watch and available documents.

Contact Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014, or call 310-663-1340 to arrange an evaluation. Cash, bank wire and business check are available for agreed purchases; confirm the payment arrangements before accepting.

Plan your evaluation in Downtown Los Angeles

Bring your items and any reports, receipts, or service records you already have. Contact us to discuss selling a luxury watch in Los Angeles and arrange an evaluation.

Evaluate a 14K white gold diamond ring in two parts: the gold alloy setting and the diamond. Then assess the complete piece, its condition and documentation. A 14K stamp or an insurance figure alone does not establish a resale offer.

In this guide

  • Read the metal description before comparing rings
  • Distinguish a finish from the ring’s construction
  • Evaluate the natural diamond separately
  • Separate metal-content arithmetic from a complete offer
  • Prepare a white gold ring for a Los Angeles evaluation

Read the metal description before comparing rings

White gold describes a gold alloy, not a separate precious metal. According to the FTC’s jewelry buying guide, 14K means 14 parts gold and 10 parts other metals, out of 24. That is approximately 58.3 percent gold by weight.

The World Gold Council’s gold jewelry guide lists the common 583 and 585 fineness designations alongside 14 karat. It also explains that white gold is alloyed with white metals and usually receives a rhodium finish. Read the complete description rather than assuming that a bright white surface establishes the underlying metal.

Distinguish a finish from the ring’s construction

Ask whether the ring is white gold throughout or has a plated base, and have unclear markings checked. A surface coating and a gold alloy setting are different things. Photograph marks inside the band if they are readable, but treat them as information for examination rather than proof that testing is unnecessary.

Look at the shank, prongs and the area underneath the center stone. Note thinning, bent parts, missing stones, previous sizing and repairs you know about. Ask a jeweler to assess a loose stone or damaged setting before continued wear. A karat number alone does not tell you how a particular ring was made or its present condition.

DetailUseful question
14K or 585 markWhat does examination establish about the metal?
White surface finishIs there rhodium plating, and what condition is it in?
Prongs and bandAre repairs or stone-security checks needed?
Maker’s markIs there documentation supporting the attribution?
Diamond paperworkWhich stone does it describe, and does it match?

Evaluate the natural diamond separately

The metal purity does not grade the diamond. Use GIA’s four quality factors to understand the reported cut, color, clarity and carat weight. Our 4 Cs guide explains how to turn those details into questions about the actual stone.

For a multi-stone ring, identify whether a stated weight concerns the center diamond or all the diamonds together. Ask what can be established while the stones remain mounted and what is estimated. Bring any existing report, and tell the evaluator about chips, replacement stones or other changes you know about.

Separate metal-content arithmetic from a complete offer

The scale weight of a finished ring includes its stones and any other components. It should not automatically be used as the weight of 14K gold. Once the relevant metal weight and purity are established, they help describe the gold content; they do not quote the purchase price of the finished ring.

Ask how the buyer considered the natural diamond, setting, condition and any supported maker attribution. If the offer is for the complete ring, do not add a separate theoretical metal amount to it as though the setting had been excluded. Our diamond resale offer comparison guide helps clarify what an amount includes.

Prepare a white gold ring for a Los Angeles evaluation

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds evaluates gold jewelry and buys natural cut and polished diamonds in any size or shape. We do not buy laboratory-grown, uncut or rough diamonds. Describe your ring and any uncertainty about its stones when you contact us.

Our address is 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014. Bring the complete piece and existing paperwork so the discussion concerns your ring rather than a generic online example.

Is 14K white gold the same as platinum?

No. They are different metal descriptions. A similar white appearance does not make their composition, markings or valuation interchangeable.

Can I price my ring from its stamp and total weight?

Those details are only a starting point. The metal needs evaluation, stone weight must be distinguished, and the natural diamond and complete ring need their own assessment.

We buy scrap gold, Cuban chains and bracelets with or without diamonds, gold coins, and silver coins. Single pieces and large quantities are welcome. Payment is available by cash, bank wire, or business check.

When choosing a 14K white gold engagement ring, compare the actual setting, alloy, finish and diamond together. Karat describes gold content; it does not guarantee a particular level of durability, stone security or maintenance.

In this guide

  • Know what 14K white gold tells you
  • Examine the setting as a structure
  • View the diamond in the complete ring
  • Plan care around the actual jewelry
  • If you are selling an existing ring

Know what 14K white gold tells you

According to the World Gold Council’s jewelry guide, 14K gold is approximately 58.3% gold combined with other metals. White gold is an alloy, often finished with rhodium. Two rings with the same karat can still differ in alloy recipe, construction and surface finish.

Ask the seller to identify the setting material and finish in writing. If you have a known metal sensitivity, ask about the actual alloy rather than treating the words “white gold” as an assurance of suitability. For a broader material comparison, read our platinum and white gold guide.

Examine the setting as a structure

Look at the ring from above, from the side and beneath the center stone. Discuss prong condition, the thickness of the band, how high the stone sits and how the ring fits beside a wedding band. A low profile, halo or narrow band changes the design questions; a single karat number does not answer them.

CheckAsk before choosing
Stone mountingHow is this particular stone supported and inspected?
Band and fitIs the size comfortable, and is future resizing practical?
Side stonesWhat care does this setting require?
FinishIs it rhodium plated, and what service is recommended?
Written specificationsAre metal, diamond details and service terms recorded?

Do not infer that every 14K setting is stronger than every 18K setting. The actual alloy, design, manufacture, wear and repairs all deserve attention. A worn prong needs examination regardless of the ring’s original specifications.

View the diamond in the complete ring

GIA explains how setting metal affects diamond color appearance through reflected surroundings. View the ring in more than one ordinary lighting condition. A bright display light or photograph may not show how the piece looks on your hand.

Keep appearance separate from documented diamond grades. Compare the diamond’s 4Cs, dimensions and report details alongside your visual preferences. Ask whether a quoted carat weight refers to the center stone or all the diamonds combined.

Plan care around the actual jewelry

A 10K white gold ring contains about 41.7 percent gold in its alloy. Compare the actual band, finish and setting condition; the karat number alone does not promise a particular lifespan, scratch resistance or resale price.

In this guide

  • Separate the gold alloy from its surface finish
  • Compare designs by their practical details
  • Discuss care for this particular ring
  • Prepare a resale evaluation

Separate the gold alloy from its surface finish

10K describes the proportion of gold: 10 parts out of 24, or approximately 41.7 percent. The World Gold Council’s purity guide explains how alloying changes gold’s color and lists the 417 fineness mark for 10 karat. White gold is usually finished with rhodium, so its surface appearance is a separate question from its gold content.

Ask for the full metal description. A white gold alloy ring and a ring with a coated base metal are different products. The FTC’s precious-metal jewelry guide helps distinguish alloy, plated and filled descriptions. Neither a bright surface nor a photograph establishes which construction you have.

Compare designs by their practical details

A plain band, a twisted design and a diamond-accent ring serve different preferences. Compare comfort and construction instead of assigning every example of one style a higher quality rating. If buying, try the actual ring and ask about sizing before paying for a design that may be difficult to alter.

DesignWhat to examine
Plain bandWidth, thickness, inner profile and signs of thinning
Twisted or openwork bandConnections, edges and the feasibility of resizing
Stone-set ringProngs, missing stones and access for inspection
Textured finishWear to the pattern and how repair would affect it

For a pre-owned ring, ask about past sizing, replaced stones and repairs. Lower gold content does not automatically make every design stronger than a higher-karat ring. The particular alloy, manufacturing work, dimensions and current condition all need consideration.

Discuss care for this particular ring

Ask the jeweler what finish is present and how it should be maintained. There is no useful universal promise that every ring needs refinishing at the same interval or will last a fixed number of years without repairs.

GIA’s jewelry-care guidance explains that chemicals can affect precious metals and that cleaning must account for the gemstones present. Describe any loose stone or damaged section before attempting cleaning. For a white-metal comparison, read our platinum and white gold guide.

Prepare a resale evaluation

Bring the ring intact with any receipt, metal description or stone report. An evaluator needs the relevant metal weight and purity; total ring weight may include diamonds or other materials. For a diamond ring, use the 10K diamond ring guide to separate metal markings from stone measurements.

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds buys gold jewelry and scrap gold at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014. We also buy natural cut and polished diamonds in any size or shape; we do not buy laboratory-grown, uncut or rough diamonds. Contact us to describe your ring and arrange its evaluation.

Does a 10K mark tell me the ring’s exact value?

No. It describes a claimed purity. Examination, relevant metal weight, condition and any stones are needed to discuss an offer for the actual piece.

Should I refinish a ring before selling it?

Ask the evaluator first. Paying for cosmetic work does not guarantee that the purchase offer will increase by the cost of that work.

We buy scrap gold, Cuban chains and bracelets with or without diamonds, gold coins, and silver coins. Single pieces and large quantities are welcome. Payment is available by cash, bank wire, or business check.

On a diamond ring, 10K describes the gold alloy’s purity. It does not mean a ten-carat diamond or a ten-thousand-dollar price. Read the diamond description and setting details separately before comparing complete-ring offers.

In this guide

  • Read three different numbers correctly
  • Look beyond the metal purity when comparing rings
  • Establish what is known about the natural diamond
  • Keep a buying budget separate from a resale expectation
  • Bring your ring to a Los Angeles buyer

Read three different numbers correctly

A ring listing can include a gold purity mark, diamond weight and price. These numbers describe different things. Write them separately when comparing pieces so an abbreviated description does not create a false impression of size or quality.

DescriptionMeaning
10K gold10 parts gold out of 24 in the stated alloy
1.00 ct diamondA stated diamond weight of one carat
Total diamond carat weightThe combined weight of the diamonds described
A dollar priceAn asking price or offer whose terms still need checking

The FTC explains gold karat descriptions. For stones, GIA defines one metric carat as 200 milligrams. Our carat-weight guide covers the distinction between a center diamond and the combined diamonds in a ring.

Look beyond the metal purity when comparing rings

10K gold contains approximately 41.7 percent gold. That identifies the gold proportion, not the ring’s design quality or the security of its setting. Ask whether the band is hollow or solid in construction, whether it has been sized and whether any repairs are recommended.

If considering white gold, ask about its finish and read our 10K white gold construction guide. Compare similar designs and actual condition rather than assuming that lower-karat gold is always stronger or cheaper as a complete finished ring.

Establish what is known about the natural diamond

GIA’s quality-factor guide explains cut, color, clarity and carat weight. Read all available information together. Clarity concerns the nature and visibility of characteristics, rather than simply the number of marks, and shape is not the same thing as cut quality.

Ask whether the stone is natural, whether a laboratory report is available and which diamond the report describes. For multiple stones, request a clear center-stone description and a separate explanation of accent stones. View the actual ring in more than one lighting condition when possible, without treating a photograph or visual impression as a laboratory grade.

Keep a buying budget separate from a resale expectation

A purchase budget should cover the complete ring and any agreed sizing or other work. Ask the seller for the full description, total price and written return terms. Avoid a generic online price range that does not identify a comparable stone and setting.

When selling, ask for an evaluation of your complete piece and a final purchase amount. The gold calculation should account for relevant metal weight, while the natural diamond receives its own consideration. An existing report can help the examination; it does not promise a fixed premium or a set percentage of the original retail price.

Bring your ring to a Los Angeles buyer

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds buys gold rings and scrap gold and natural cut and polished diamonds in any size or shape. We do not buy laboratory-grown, uncut or rough diamonds. Bring available paperwork to 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014, or contact us before visiting.

Can the whole ring’s scale weight be used as its gold weight?

Not automatically. The total includes the stones and any other components, which need to be distinguished from the gold alloy being assessed.

Does choosing 10K guarantee a lower complete-ring price?

No. The diamond, design, workmanship, condition and seller’s terms also affect the price of a finished ring.

We buy scrap gold, Cuban chains and bracelets with or without diamonds, gold coins, and silver coins. Single pieces and large quantities are welcome. Payment is available by cash, bank wire, or business check.
