Before mailing gold, confirm the buyer’s identity, current receiving instructions, coverage for your exact items, return conditions and payment process. Keep an item inventory and shipping records. An online estimate remains preliminary until the actual collection is examined.

In this guide

  • Confirm the process with the buyer first
  • Make an inventory you can match to the offer
  • Check coverage for the actual contents
  • Keep evidence through delivery and evaluation
  • Compare the final amount with its assumptions
  • Understand acceptance, returns and payment

Confirm the process with the buyer first

Contact the business through its verified website or phone number and ask whether it currently accepts your item type by mail. Obtain the correct receiving instructions and written terms before sending anything. A storefront address or an old article is not enough to establish a mail-in arrangement.

For Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds, call 310-663-1340 or contact us to discuss your collection and the available evaluation arrangements. In-person evaluations are available in Downtown Los Angeles.

Make an inventory you can match to the offer

List the pieces, visible markings, identifying details and known damage. Photograph the items and keep matching reports or documents identifiable. For mixed gold, group marked pieces where practical and leave uncertain items for examination.

Keep stones and detached parts with their matching jewelry. Avoid dismantling a diamond chain or polishing a potentially collectible coin solely for shipping. Our scrap-gold guide covers mixed pieces and broken chains.

Check coverage for the actual contents

Ask who provides coverage, which jewelry or precious-metal items qualify, the applicable value limit, exclusions, packaging conditions and who handles a claim. A shipping label or tracking number alone does not answer those questions.

USPS Registered Mail guidance, for example, distinguishes declared value and applicable coverage requirements. Check the rules of the actual service being used; do not assume every carrier or mail class treats jewelry, coins and bullion alike.

Keep evidence through delivery and evaluation

Follow the agreed packaging instructions and retain the inventory, acceptance receipt and tracking information. Save proof of value appropriate to the chosen service. USPS claim rules illustrate why insurance and value records matter if a shipment is lost or damaged.

Confirm who acknowledges receipt and how your items will be identified in the evaluation. For a large collection, discuss quantity and any special handling before dispatch.

Compare the final amount with its assumptions

A dated gold-price reference can help explain a metal input, but an online calculator cannot verify your items. Ask about tested purity, net weight, stones and any complete-jewelry resale consideration.

Use our offer checklist to distinguish a preliminary estimate from the final amount after any charges and remaining checks.

Understand acceptance, returns and payment

Before shipping, establish how to decline, any response deadline, return costs and return coverage. Ask whether any procedure could alter the items and obtain an explanation before agreeing. Keep the terms with your inventory.

If you accept an offer, confirm when and how payment will be issued. Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds offers cash, bank wire and business-check payment; discuss which method fits the agreed transaction. Our local versus online comparison helps you decide which evaluation process suits you.

Plan your evaluation in Downtown Los Angeles

We buy scrap gold, Cuban chains and bracelets with or without diamonds, gold coins, and silver coins. Single pieces and large quantities are welcome. Payment is available by cash, bank wire, or business check.

Call 310-663-1340 ↗

A local evaluation lets you discuss the actual pieces in person. A mail-in evaluation adds shipping, coverage, receipt and return arrangements. Neither channel guarantees a higher purchase amount: compare final offers for the same items and review all conditions.

In this guide

  • Choose the process that fits your collection
  • Compare the practical steps
  • For shipping, read the applicable coverage terms
  • For a local visit, prepare the questions in advance
  • Compare the final purchase amounts
  • Discuss an evaluation with Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds

Choose the process that fits your collection

A small group of ordinary gold pieces and a mixed estate collection can need different amounts of explanation. Consider whether you want to discuss the items in person, how easily you can visit a buyer and whether shipping terms cover the entire collection.

Gold with diamonds, collectible coins and signed jewelry needs more than a gross-weight estimate. Keep those characteristics visible whichever channel you choose.

Compare the practical steps

QuestionLocal visitMail-in evaluation
How do items reach the buyer?You arrange a visit with the collection.You agree on shipping and receipt instructions.
How do you ask about the evaluation?Discuss the items during the visit.Confirm the contact and reporting process.
What if you decline?Clarify any evaluation terms before starting.Check return cost, timing, coverage and deadlines in advance.
When is payment available?Confirm the agreed method and timing.Confirm the agreed method and timing after acceptance.

These are process differences, not a ranking of buyers. A high preliminary quote in either channel still needs verification of the actual pieces.

For shipping, read the applicable coverage terms

Check that the exact item types and declared value qualify for the chosen service. Ask about exclusions, packaging, proof of value and claims responsibility. USPS Registered Mail guidance provides one example of service-specific requirements; another service may use different terms.

Use the online-selling checklist before sending a collection. Tracking is useful evidence but does not replace agreed coverage and return arrangements.

For a local visit, prepare the questions in advance

Bring matching documents and detached parts, and identify pieces you want to keep. Ask how different purities and non-gold components will be considered. Discuss any proposed procedure that could alter the jewelry before agreeing.

Our first-evaluation guide walks through a Downtown Los Angeles visit. Call ahead for a large quantity of scrap, heavy Cuban chains or gold and silver coins.

Compare the final purchase amounts

Record the same pieces, tested material, applicable weight, charges and outstanding checks. A dated gold-price reference informs the metal input but cannot determine every jewelry offer. Shipping or return costs can also matter to the overall comparison.

Ask whether the proposal is an outright purchase, loan, trade-in or consignment. Those arrangements should not be compared as though they all produce the same purchase payment.

html:
Use the actual length, width and depth of the 3.5-carat oval, then inspect its appearance in movement and in the intended setting. Carat weight and a preferred length-to-width ratio alone do not establish size on the hand or cut quality.

In this guide

  • Confirm the weight and actual dimensions
  • Use the ratio to describe shape, not certify quality
  • View the bow tie and light pattern in movement
  • Read the report without inventing a cut grade
  • Try the complete ring and confirm the transaction

Confirm the weight and actual dimensions

A 3.5-carat diamond weighs 0.7 grams using GIA’s definition of 200 milligrams per carat. That does not prescribe its length and width. Read the measurements for the actual stone instead of assuming every oval of that weight is the same size.

Establish whether 3.5 carats describes the center diamond or the combined diamonds in the ring. A halo or side stones can change the total-weight description without changing the center stone. Our carat-weight guide explains the wording to check.

Use the ratio to describe shape, not certify quality

Divide the recorded length by the width to describe how elongated the oval is. A higher ratio indicates a longer outline relative to its width. Decide which outline you prefer by looking at actual examples; there is no single ratio that guarantees a pleasing result for every person or setting.

GIA’s oval diamond guide discusses shape proportions, girdle information and the bow-tie effect. These details need to be considered together. A preferred outline cannot substitute for examining the stone’s appearance.

View the bow tie and light pattern in movement

The dark contrast often called a bow tie can change with viewing position and the light blocked by the observer. Inspect the oval at a normal viewing distance and move it gently. A single photograph can emphasize or hide a particular pattern.

Compare examples under similar conditions. Note whether a central dark area dominates your view and whether the appearance changes as you move. Ask for additional viewing when a photograph or short video does not show enough. Keep that visual assessment separate from the grades recorded on the report.

Read the report without inventing a cut grade

GIA’s sample diamond reports show the information available from different services. The overall GIA cut grade used for standard round brilliant D-to-Z diamonds should not be assumed to apply to an oval. Read polish, symmetry, measurements and comments in their own fields.

Do not treat a chosen clarity grade as a promise that every characteristic will be invisible. Examine the stone and ask what the report describes. The 4 Cs guide helps separate those questions.

Try the complete ring and confirm the transaction

CheckQuestion for the jeweler
Ring profileHow high will the stone sit on the hand?
SettingHow is this particular stone supported and protected?
Band fitIs the ring comfortable and compatible with an adjacent band?
Written descriptionDoes it identify the center stone and all included work?

If selling, preserve the complete ring and bring existing records. Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds buys natural cut and polished diamonds in any size or shape; we do not buy laboratory-grown, uncut or rough diamonds. Contact us or visit 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014.

Does a 3.5-carat oval always measure 11.5 by 8 millimeters?

No. Use the actual report measurements. Weight does not specify one mandatory outline or depth.

Does an ideal-looking ratio guarantee a well-cut oval?

No. Ratio describes outline. Examine the full stone, its light pattern, condition and report information.

Plan your evaluation in Downtown Los Angeles

Bring your items and any reports, receipts, or service records you already have. Contact us to discuss selling diamonds in Los Angeles and arrange an evaluation.

Compare complete quotes for specifically described two-carat diamonds and settings. Weight alone does not set the price, and a ring labeled two carats total can contain several smaller diamonds instead of a two-carat center stone.

In this guide

  • Confirm that the descriptions refer to the same thing
  • Compare the actual natural diamonds
  • Read dimensions and report fields in context
  • Request a complete written quote
  • Use a different comparison when selling

Confirm that the descriptions refer to the same thing

A two-carat center diamond and a ring with two carats of diamonds combined are different products. Ask which weight is being advertised before comparing prices. The presence of side stones or a halo should be described separately from the center diamond.

GIA defines a metric carat as 200 milligrams, so a two-carat diamond weighs 0.4 grams. Weight is not a face-up measurement. Two stones of the same carat weight can have different dimensions and shapes; our carat-weight guide explains how to read both.

Compare the actual natural diamonds

Record the laboratory, report number, shape, measurements and quality information for each candidate. GIA’s quality-factor guide explains why cut, color, clarity and carat should be considered together. A two-carat label alone is not a comparable specification.

View the stone when possible and ask about the characteristics described on its report. Do not assume that every diamond at a selected clarity grade will look identical or that a color range will appear colorless to every observer. For an oval, compare its actual outline and light pattern using the questions in our oval diamond guide.

Read dimensions and report fields in context

GIA’s sample reports illustrate how measurements, quality information and comments are recorded. A chart showing one approximate dimension for each shape is only an illustration; it does not establish the dimensions of the diamond offered to you.

Ask which cut information is supplied for that shape. Do not treat polish or symmetry as though either were an overall cut grade. For a mounted stone, clarify whether a quoted weight is measured or estimated and what records support it.

Request a complete written quote

Quote detailWhat to confirm
Center diamondThe specific stone, report and agreed description
Setting and side stonesMetal, design, additional diamonds and included components
Sizing or custom workScope, completion expectations and charges
Total amountAll applicable charges included in the transaction
Return and change termsWhat applies to the stone and any custom work

Compare alternatives within the budget you choose. A stone slightly below two carats may be worth considering, but do not assume a guaranteed discount or an identical appearance. Obtain actual descriptions and quotes for the options in front of you.

Use a different comparison when selling

A retail quote concerns buying a ring. A resale offer concerns what a buyer will pay for your existing piece under stated terms. Use our diamond resale offer guide to compare the same complete item, deductions and payment conditions.

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds buys natural cut and polished diamonds in any size or shape. We do not buy laboratory-grown, uncut or rough diamonds. Bring your ring and existing paperwork to 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014, or contact us at 310-663-1340.

Should a two-carat diamond cost exactly twice a one-carat diamond?

No. Weight is only one part of the description. Compare the actual stones and transaction terms instead of applying a multiplication rule.

Does a two-carat total ring contain one two-carat diamond?

Not necessarily. Total weight combines the diamonds specified in the description. Ask for the center stone’s individual weight.

Bring your items and any reports, receipts, or service records you already have. Contact us to discuss selling diamonds in Los Angeles and arrange an evaluation.

Before buying or selling a diamond watch, check its identity, the stones, the origin of the setting, the materials, current condition, matching records and transaction terms. Resolve unknowns before treating a description or estimate as a final agreement.

In this guide

  • 1. What exact watch is being described?
  • 2. What is known about the stones?
  • 3. Who supplied the setting?
  • 4. What are the case and bracelet made from?
  • 5. What is the present condition?
  • 6. Which records and accessories belong to it?
  • 7. What exactly are the transaction terms?
  • Prepare a Downtown Los Angeles evaluation

1. What exact watch is being described?

Request the maker, reference and configuration. Match the description to the physical watch rather than a similar stock image. A recognizable logo or model nickname is not enough to establish the complete item.

2. What is known about the stones?

Ask whether they are identified as natural diamonds, laboratory-grown diamonds or another material, and what supports that description. GIA discusses the examination needed to distinguish natural and laboratory-grown diamonds.

Do not infer identity from sparkle. If the watch contains many stones, ask whether a stated carat weight is a documented total or an estimate. The diamond quality factors explained by GIA help clarify the terms without assigning a purchase price.

3. Who supplied the setting?

Separate a manufacturer gem-set configuration from a later custom bezel, dial or bracelet. Ask for records of alterations and replacement components. “Factory” in a listing should be supported, not accepted simply because the watch carries a brand name.

4. What are the case and bracelet made from?

Check each component's material rather than assuming everything is gold. The FTC's precious-metal terminology distinguishes alloys from surface coatings. Whole-watch weight cannot be treated as pure-gold weight.

5. What is the present condition?

Discuss operation, known repairs, loose stones, bracelet wear and missing links. Agree before any opening, removal or further work. Do not arrange polishing or gem replacement merely because you assume it will improve resale proceeds.

6. Which records and accessories belong to it?

List the box, warranty documents, service invoices, stone reports and spare links included. A report or invoice should match the relevant watch or component. Missing records are a question to discuss, not a reason to invent its history.

Our diamond watch evaluation guide explains why watch authenticity, natural stone identity and setting originality are separate issues.

7. What exactly are the transaction terms?

Confirm the final amount, included items, unresolved inspection conditions and payment arrangements. For a purchase from a seller, read any return and warranty terms. For a sale to a buyer, distinguish an outright offer from a consignment estimate.

No watch or diamond setting guarantees appreciation. Compare the actual proposal with your objectives. The watch selling-options guide helps compare transaction routes.

Prepare a Downtown Los Angeles evaluation

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds buys natural, cut and polished diamonds of any size or shape, including in luxury watches. We do not buy laboratory-grown, uncut or rough diamonds. Explain any alterations and bring available records.

Contact Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014, or call 310-663-1340 to arrange an evaluation. Cash, bank wire and business check are available for agreed purchases; confirm the payment arrangements before accepting.

Plan your evaluation in Downtown Los Angeles

Bring your items and any reports, receipts, or service records you already have. Contact us to discuss selling a luxury watch in Los Angeles and arrange an evaluation.

Selling a luxury watch in Los Angeles · 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014

Call 310-663-1340 ↗

  • FTC: precious-metal jewelry descriptions

Sell Your Rolex Watch in Los Angeles

Rolex is one of the most recognized names in the luxury watch resale market, but the value of one Rolex can differ significantly from another.

When evaluating a Rolex, relevant factors can include the model, reference number, production period, condition, dial, bracelet, materials, originality, box and papers, service history, and current demand for that particular configuration.

Popular Rolex collections can include models such as the Submariner, Daytona, GMT-Master II, Datejust, Day-Date, Explorer, Yacht-Master, and others.

If you have the original Rolex box, warranty card, papers, receipt, service records, or extra bracelet links, bring them with the watch.

We Buy More Than Rolex

Luxury watch value extends well beyond Rolex. We also evaluate watches from other desirable manufacturers, including Cartier, Audemars Piguet, Patek Philippe, Omega, Breitling, and other luxury brands based on current market demand.

Depending on the watch, important factors may include the specific collection, reference number, case material, dial configuration, movement, condition, originality, age, accessories, and current secondary-market demand.

What Determines the Value of a Luxury Watch?

There is no single price guide that determines what every luxury watch is worth. The value of a particular watch depends on several characteristics working together.

Brand and Model

Certain manufacturers, collections, and references have stronger secondary-market demand than others.

Reference Number

The exact reference can identify important differences between watches that may initially look very similar.

Condition

Case, bracelet, crystal, dial, bezel, movement, and overall wear can affect desirability and value.

Originality

Original components can matter to collectors. Replacement or aftermarket components may influence an evaluation depending on the watch.

Materials

Stainless steel, gold, platinum, two-tone construction, diamonds, and other materials can affect the value of a watch.

Box and Papers

Original warranty cards, certificates, boxes, receipts, manuals, hang tags, service records, and extra links can be helpful when evaluating provenance and completeness.

Current Market Demand

Luxury watch resale markets change. Demand for specific brands, models, references, dial configurations, sizes, and materials can influence what buyers are willing to pay.

How We Evaluate a Luxury Watch

A luxury watch evaluation can involve examining identifying characteristics of the watch, including its case, dial, bracelet, movement when appropriate, reference information, materials, condition, and other details.

The purpose is to understand exactly what watch is being presented and the factors relevant to its current resale market. Some watches may require additional authentication or research before an evaluation can be completed.

What Should I Bring When Selling My Watch?

  • The watch
  • Original box, if available
  • Warranty card or papers, if available
  • Original purchase receipt, if available
  • Service records
  • Extra bracelet links
  • Additional straps or accessories originally supplied with the watch
  • Relevant documentation

Do not worry if you no longer have every accessory. Bring the watch and whatever documentation or accessories remain, and we can determine what information is relevant during the evaluation.

Selling a Luxury Watch Locally vs. Online

Owners have several options when selling a luxury watch, including a direct local buyer, online marketplace, consignment company, or auction house.

Direct Local Watch Buyer

A local direct buyer allows the watch to be examined in person and gives the owner an opportunity to consider an item-specific offer without first shipping the watch to an unknown destination.

Online Marketplace

Selling directly to another consumer may require creating a listing, photographing the watch, communicating with buyers, handling payment, shipping, returns, and platform requirements.

Consignment

With consignment, the watch is generally marketed to another purchaser before the owner receives proceeds. Fees and timelines vary by company.

Auction

Auctions may be appropriate for certain rare or collectible watches, but fees, reserves, schedules, and results vary depending on the auction house and specific watch.

Compare the Final Offer for Your Actual Watch

When comparing luxury watch buyers, an early estimate is not necessarily the same thing as the final offer for the actual watch.

The watch’s exact reference, condition, originality, accessories, and other characteristics may not be fully known until the watch is examined.

Before deciding where to sell, consider the final item-specific offer and ask how the buyer arrived at the valuation.

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds buys natural, cut and polished diamonds in Downtown Los Angeles—any size, any shape, loose or set in jewelry. We welcome large individual diamonds, engagement rings, eternity bands, estate pieces and collections. We buy natural diamonds only. We do not buy laboratory-grown, uncut or rough diamonds.

Have a substantial stone or diamond collection? See our large natural diamond buying guide for the shapes, jewelry and documents to bring.

If your diamond has a GIA grading report or other documentation, bring it with you. Documentation can help us verify important characteristics of the stone, but we can also evaluate diamonds that do not have their original paperwork.

After evaluating your diamond, we can provide an offer based on the specific stone and current resale market conditions. There is no obligation to sell simply because you receive an evaluation.

What Types of Diamonds Do We Buy in Los Angeles?

We buy natural polished diamonds of any size and shape, including these loose stones and jewelry pieces:

  • GIA-graded diamonds
  • Loose diamonds
  • Natural diamonds
  • Engagement rings
  • Diamond wedding rings
  • Diamond earrings
  • Diamond necklaces
  • Diamond bracelets
  • Estate and inherited diamond jewelry
  • Vintage diamond jewelry
  • Designer diamond jewelry
  • Diamonds set in gold or platinum jewelry

If you are unsure what you have, bring the item in for evaluation rather than trying to determine its value from photographs or online calculators alone.

Schedule Your Diamond Evaluation

Book a private appointment online, call us, or visit our Downtown Los Angeles location for an in-person diamond evaluation.

Expert Diamond Evaluation

We examine your diamond’s carat weight, cut, color, clarity, shape, condition, certification, and other factors that can affect its resale value.

Receive Your Offer

After the evaluation, we explain our offer so you can decide whether selling your diamond is right for you. Cash, bank wire and business-check payment are available for agreed purchases. Confirm the payment arrangements before accepting.

Speak With Us

Understanding Your Diamond Before You Sell

Selling a GIA Diamond in Los Angeles

A GIA grading report can provide important information about a diamond, including its carat weight, color, clarity, cut grade when applicable, measurements, proportions, and identifying characteristics.

If your diamond has its original GIA report, bring the report with you. We can use the grading information together with an inspection of the actual diamond and current market conditions when evaluating the stone.

A grading report does not by itself determine the amount a buyer will pay. Two diamonds with similar laboratory grades can have different resale demand and market values depending on characteristics such as shape, measurements, cut quality, fluorescence, condition, and current buyer demand.

How Is a Diamond’s Value Determined?

There is no single price-per-carat number that accurately values every diamond. Several characteristics work together to influence resale value.

Carat Weight

A diamond’s carat weight measures its weight, but larger diamonds do not simply increase in value at the same rate per carat. Size thresholds, quality, shape, and market demand can significantly affect value.

Cut

Cut and proportions affect how effectively a diamond reflects light and can influence both appearance and market desirability.

Color

For many colorless diamonds, less visible body color can affect grading and market value. Fancy-color diamonds are evaluated differently.

Clarity

Clarity considers inclusions and blemishes, including their size, number, position, and visibility.

Other important factors can include diamond shape, measurements, fluorescence, laboratory report, condition, brand or setting, and current wholesale and resale demand.

Sell Your Diamond Engagement Ring in Los Angeles

If you are selling a diamond engagement ring, we evaluate both the center diamond and the ring itself. Depending on the piece, factors such as additional diamonds, precious-metal content, designer branding, condition, and documentation may also affect the overall evaluation.

Bring any GIA reports, receipts, original boxes, designer documentation, or other paperwork you still have. These items are helpful when available, but they are not required for us to examine your jewelry.

Speak With Us

Why Sell Your Diamond to Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds?

Our goal is to make selling a diamond in Los Angeles straightforward and transparent. You can bring your diamond to our Downtown Los Angeles Jewelry District location for an in-person evaluation and receive an offer based on the characteristics of your specific item and current market conditions.

There is no obligation to sell after receiving an evaluation.

  • In-person diamond evaluation
  • Downtown Los Angeles Jewelry District location
  • Natural diamonds evaluated with or without existing grading reports
  • Loose diamonds and diamond jewelry accepted
  • Engagement rings and estate jewelry evaluated
  • Clear explanation of the offer
  • No obligation to sell

Read our customer reviews to learn about other sellers’ experiences.

Get an Item-Specific Diamond Offer

When comparing diamond buyers, focus on the final offer for your actual diamond rather than relying only on an estimated price given before the stone is inspected.

A diamond’s value cannot be determined accurately from carat weight alone. The complete characteristics of the diamond and current market demand matter.

Ask how the offer was determined and compare final, item-specific offers before deciding where to sell.

Local Diamond Buyer vs. Consignment or Auction

There are several ways to sell a diamond. The right choice depends on whether your priority is convenience, speed, or potentially waiting for a future buyer.

Direct Local Diamond Buyer

A direct buyer evaluates the diamond and can make an offer for the item. This allows the seller to decide whether to accept an offer without waiting for the jewelry to sell to another consumer.

Consignment

With consignment, the jewelry is generally listed for sale and the seller waits for another buyer to purchase it. Terms, fees, and timelines vary by company.

Auction

Auction may be appropriate for certain rare, important, or highly desirable pieces. Auction fees, timing, reserves, and results vary depending on the auction house and item.

Have other items to sell? We also evaluate gold jewelry and luxury watches.

Where can I sell a diamond in Los Angeles?

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds evaluates diamonds at our location in the Downtown Los Angeles Jewelry District. We evaluate loose diamonds, engagement rings, diamond jewelry, estate pieces, and GIA-graded diamonds.

Do I need a GIA certificate to sell my diamond?

No. A GIA report or other laboratory documentation is helpful when available, but you can still bring a diamond for evaluation without its original paperwork.

What determines how much my diamond is worth?

Diamond value can depend on carat weight, cut, color, clarity, shape, measurements, condition, laboratory grading, fluorescence, and current resale demand.

Do you buy loose diamonds?

Yes. We buy loose natural polished diamonds of any size and shape, as well as natural diamonds in engagement rings and other jewelry. We do not buy laboratory-grown or uncut diamonds.

Can I sell an engagement ring?

Yes. We evaluate diamond engagement rings and consider the center stone as well as relevant characteristics of the setting, additional stones, precious metals, branding, condition, and documentation.

Should I bring my GIA report?

Yes, if you have it. Bring the original GIA report and any other relevant documentation, receipts, boxes, or designer paperwork that may help identify the item.

How do I compare offers from diamond buyers?

Compare the final offer for your actual diamond and ask how the buyer determined the offer. Estimates given before physical inspection may change after the diamond’s characteristics are verified.

Is a diamond evaluation the same as an insurance appraisal?

Not necessarily. An insurance or replacement-value appraisal serves a different purpose from an offer to purchase a diamond in the current resale market.

10KT and 10K describe the same nominal purity: 10 parts gold out of 24, about 41.67%. The quantity of gold depends on the verified alloy weight. Stones, construction, condition and the complete piece can also affect an actual purchase offer.

In this guide

  • Read 10KT as a purity description
  • Count the applicable alloy, not every component
  • Distinguish an alloy from a gold surface
  • Consider intact jewelry before calling it scrap
  • Compare a current offer with the right reference
  • Sell 10K jewelry and scrap in Downtown LA

Read 10KT as a purity description

10KT is another way to write 10 karat. A 417 fineness mark corresponds to approximately 41.7% gold. The World Gold Council explains common purity and fineness descriptions.

The remaining alloy is not necessarily all copper. Ingredients can differ by maker and color, and a mark alone does not verify the material. Keep unmarked or uncertain pieces for professional examination rather than guessing.

Count the applicable alloy, not every component

If a bracelet contains 24 grams of verified 10K alloy after non-alloy parts are excluded, its nominal gold content is ten grams: 24 × 10 ÷ 24. A 24-gram whole-item reading with stones or other components is a different starting point.

For mixed pieces, keep purity groups separate. Do not apply a 14K rate to a 10K item or multiply an already adjusted 10K buying rate by the purity fraction a second time. Our 10K per-gram guide explains rate comparisons.

Distinguish an alloy from a gold surface

The FTC describes gold-plated and gold-filled products separately from gold-alloy jewelry. A plated item's full weight cannot be used as though the entire item were a 10K alloy.

Hollow construction is another question: a genuine alloy chain can have hollow links and weigh less than a similar-looking solid chain. Appearance, width and heft cannot supply a precise gold-content measurement.

Consider intact jewelry before calling it scrap

A broken clasp does not eliminate the gold still present. However, a ring's setting, a bracelet's maker and the condition of a complete jewel can affect whether it has a practical resale use beyond material content.

Bring diamond reports, receipts and detached parts if available. For everyday rings, our 10K ring guide covers material, construction and stone questions. The scrap-gold checklist helps organize damaged pieces.

Compare a current offer with the right reference

A dated market-price reference helps estimate contained-gold value. A retail receipt includes a different transaction and does not establish a fixed resale return. Neither a gold-price forecast nor an advertised payout percentage guarantees the final amount.

Ask which pieces the offer includes, how the material was assessed and whether further checks or charges remain. Compare final amounts for the same collection before deciding.

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds buys 10K jewelry, broken pieces and heavy chains, including substantial collections. Arrange an evaluation at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014, and discuss cash, bank wire or business-check payment.

Plan your evaluation in Downtown Los Angeles

We buy scrap gold, Cuban chains and bracelets with or without diamonds, gold coins, and silver coins. Single pieces and large quantities are welcome. Payment is available by cash, bank wire, or business check.

html:
About Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds

A local buying service in the Downtown Los Angeles Jewelry District, at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014.

What we buy

We buy gold jewelry, scrap gold, Cuban chains and gold or silver coins, natural polished diamonds and luxury watches. Single items and larger collections are welcome.

Natural, cut and polished diamonds of any size or shape may be loose or set in jewelry. We do not buy laboratory-grown, uncut or rough diamonds. Our gemstone buying is limited to large, high-quality stones, including green Colombian emeralds, Burmese rubies and Ceylon blue sapphires. Certificates are welcome but not required.

Understand your purchase evaluation

Bring the complete items and any records you already have. The discussion should distinguish what has been verified, what remains uncertain and what is included in the offer. A purchase evaluation is different from a formal appraisal for insurance, tax or another specified purpose.

A preliminary phone or photo estimate can change when the actual item's weight, purity, authenticity, condition and other features are examined. Review the final net amount and payment terms before accepting. Cash, bank wire and business check are available for agreed purchases.

Arrange a visit

Call 310-663-1340 to discuss your items and availability. Confirm building access and the documents needed for your transaction. If you are considering shipping, request current receiving and return instructions before sending any valuables.

Contact and appointment options ↗

html:
Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds · Downtown Los Angeles

Sell Estate, Inherited & Antique Jewelry in Los Angeles

Sorting inherited jewelry or considering selling an older piece? Bring the jewelry and its available records to our Downtown Los Angeles location for an item-specific purchase evaluation.

We consider the actual materials, condition and complete-piece characteristics. A family description, old receipt or photograph can help the discussion, but it does not establish authenticity, age or the final offer.

Arrange an estate jewelry evaluation ↗Call 310-663-1340

617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014. Call before travelling to confirm availability and what to bring.

Your piecesThe evaluationWhat to bringQuestions

Start with the jewelry you actually have

Estate, inherited and antique describe different aspects of a piece. Previously owned jewelry can be recent; inherited jewelry may span several generations. A period-inspired design is not proof of age or maker. Note what you know and preserve the records that support it.

Gold and natural diamond jewelry

Rings, necklaces, bracelets, earrings and broken gold pieces may have metal, stone and complete-piece characteristics to consider. Keep matching sets and detached parts together.

Signed, vintage or possible antique pieces

Bring pieces intact, with receipts, boxes and maker information where available. A signature, unusual setting or family history is a starting point for examination, not a guaranteed premium.

Inherited Rolex and luxury watches

Keep the watch with its bracelet links, box, papers and service records. Disclose repairs or replacement parts. Read our Rolex and luxury watch buying information.

Mixed collections and loose stones

Describe the collection before visiting so we can discuss which pieces fit our service. Set aside items you want to retain and identify any uncertain materials.

Our buying scope includes gold jewelry and scrap, natural, cut and polished diamonds, luxury watches and large, high-quality gemstones. We do not buy laboratory-grown, uncut or rough diamonds. Age alone does not make every object suitable for purchase.

For more on preserving older pieces, see our antique gold jewelry selling guide.

How a complete-piece evaluation works

  1. Identify the selection and its records

    Show which pieces are available to sell and which documents belong to each item. Explain known repairs, altered settings, replaced stones or uncertain details.

  2. Examine materials and condition

    Metal content and weight, natural diamonds, construction, wear, maker markings and supporting records can affect the proposal. Ask what has been verified and what remains uncertain. Discuss any test that could mark or alter a piece before proceeding.

  3. Review the purchase offer

    Ask whether the offer considers the complete piece or primarily its materials, which items are included and whether deductions apply. An asking price seen online is not evidence that a comparable item sold for that amount.

A preliminary estimate is not the final offer

A phone description or photograph may support an initial estimate. The final in-person offer can differ after purity, weight, condition, authenticity, construction, stones and other characteristics are verified. Compare final net amounts for the same selection of pieces.

What to bring and what to preserve

  • Complete jewelry, pairs, matching sets and detached components.
  • Available receipts, reports, prior appraisals, repair records and original boxes, matched to the correct item.
  • Your own inventory and photographs, with uncertain details identified.
  • A clear list of pieces you are considering selling and pieces you plan to keep.
  • The identification and ownership documents confirmed when arranging the visit.

Do not polish, dismantle or discard components solely to prepare a sale. A signed or antique piece may need consideration as a complete object before treating it as scrap. Our estate jewelry inventory guide explains how to organize the collection.

Purchase offer or formal appraisal?

A current purchase offer states what a buyer proposes to pay for specified items under stated terms. An appraisal for insurance, estate administration or tax documentation has a different purpose. Confirm the requirements with the professional requesting that document; a buyer’s informal evaluation may not satisfy them.

Before selling for an estate or another person, establish who has authority to make the decision and confirm the documents needed. Read our inherited jewelry documentation guide.

Decide what to keep and compare the same items

You can identify only the pieces you are considering selling. Separate financial considerations from sentimental decisions and ask for terms for that exact selection. A historical retail receipt or insurance replacement figure is not a promised resale payment.

Cash, bank wire and business check are available for agreed purchases. Confirm the payment method and timing before accepting. Our guides to comparing estate jewelry purchase offers and deciding whether to sell inherited jewelry can help you prepare questions.

Questions about selling inherited and antique jewelry

Where can I sell inherited jewelry in Los Angeles?

Contact Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014. Call 310-663-1340 to describe the pieces and arrange an in-person purchase evaluation in the Downtown Jewelry District.

Is every piece of estate jewelry an antique?

No. Estate jewelry refers to previously owned pieces; inherited describes how someone received them. Neither description establishes age. An antique-style design also does not prove when a piece was made. Keep any records and describe uncertain details as unknown.

Can I bring jewelry if I do not know the stones or maker?

Yes, describe what you have when arranging a visit. Bring complete pieces and any records rather than guessing their materials or origin. Acceptance and an offer depend on the actual items and our buying scope.

Should I clean or repair antique jewelry before selling?

Keep the pieces intact and ask before cleaning, polishing, repairing or removing stones. Alterations can affect markings, surfaces, settings and other evidence needed to evaluate a complete piece.

Do I need a formal appraisal before asking for a purchase offer?

A purchase evaluation and a formal appraisal have different purposes. Bring any report you already have. If a document is needed for estate administration, insurance or another purpose, confirm its requirements with the professional requesting it.

Does an old appraisal determine the price I will receive?

No. The report’s date, purpose and description matter, and an insurance replacement figure is not a guaranteed resale payment. A current offer depends on the inspected item and the proposed purchase terms.

Can I sell only part of an inherited collection?

Identify the pieces you are considering selling and keep those you want to retain separate. Request an offer for that exact selection, and confirm your authority to sell before agreeing to a transaction.

Can a phone estimate change after the jewelry is examined?

Yes. A preliminary discussion relies on the description or photographs available. The final in-person offer can change after materials, purity, weight, condition, authenticity, construction and other characteristics are verified.

Plan your Downtown Los Angeles visit

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds
617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014
310-663-1340

Coming from elsewhere in Los Angeles? The in-person evaluation takes place at our Downtown Jewelry District location. Call ahead about a larger collection and confirm availability, building access and the documents to bring.

Book an appointment ↗

Get directions ↗

html:
FAQ

Questions About Selling Gold, Diamonds & Watches

How do I prepare items for sale?

Bring complete items and any existing records. Avoid aggressive cleaning, polishing or removing stones before discussing the evaluation. Call to confirm identification and ownership requirements.

What sets your prices?

The offer depends on the actual item, verified materials, condition and current resale conditions. Ask what is included, what remains uncertain and the final net purchase amount.

Can I sell an item bought in another country?
Absolutely. We handle items from all over the world, appreciating the global nature of precious metals, diamonds, and watches.
Is my transaction confidential?

Ask how information needed for your transaction is collected, used and retained. Please avoid sending identification or banking information in an initial email. See our website privacy information and discuss transaction-specific questions with the store.

Do you charge for evaluations?

Call to confirm the service and any charges before your visit. A purchase evaluation and a formal written appraisal have different purposes. There is no obligation to sell simply because you request an evaluation.

What we buy

Which gemstones do you buy?

We buy only large, high-quality gemstones, including green Colombian emeralds, Burmese rubies and Ceylon blue sapphires. Certificates are welcome but not required.

Do I need a gemstone certificate?

No. A certificate or laboratory report is welcome but is not required to request an evaluation. Bring the stone or complete jewelry and whatever information you already have.

Can color prove a gemstone’s origin?

No. Share the source of an origin description, such as a laboratory report, receipt or family history. The actual stone needs examination; appearance alone does not establish geographic origin.

Does the gemstone size requirement apply to diamonds?

We buy natural, cut and polished diamonds of any size or shape, loose or in jewelry. We do not buy laboratory-grown, uncut or rough diamonds.

How can I receive payment?

Cash, bank wire and business check are available for agreed purchases. Confirm the final amount and payment arrangements before accepting.

html:
Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds · Downtown Los Angeles

Gold Buyer Los Angeles — Sell Gold Jewelry, Scrap & Coins

Bring your gold to 617 S. Hill Street for an in-person purchase evaluation. We buy gold jewelry, broken pieces, scrap gold and gold coins, from a single ring to a larger collection.

Your offer depends on the actual items: verified gold content and weight, diamonds, condition, authenticity and other resale characteristics. Review the amount and payment terms before deciding whether to sell.

Arrange a gold evaluation ↗Call 310-663-1340

Cash, bank wire, or business check for agreed purchases. Confirm payment arrangements when booking.

What we buyGold purityYour offerPlan your visitQuestions

Gold jewelry, scrap and coins

What gold can you sell?

Bring complete pieces, even if you think they are only worth their metal content. A maker, setting, collectible feature or natural diamond may need consideration before an item is treated as scrap.

Gold jewelry

Rings, necklaces, earrings, heavy Cuban chains and bracelets, with or without diamonds. Yellow, white and rose gold can all contain gold; color alone does not establish purity.

Broken jewelry & scrap gold

A broken clasp, damaged chain or single earring does not eliminate the gold content. Keep mixed pieces together and let the evaluation establish their purity and metal weight.

Gold coins & bullion

Bring gold coins in their holders and packaging. For bars or other bullion, call with the format and quantity before visiting so we can confirm whether we can evaluate your items.

Estate & designer jewelry

Inherited pieces and signed jewelry may have characteristics beyond melt value. Bring receipts, maker information and existing reports. Do not remove stones or polish away markings before the visit.

Large quantities are welcome. We also buy silver coins. Call ahead about larger collections to arrange enough time. Read our Downtown LA gold coin selling guide and estate jewelry service.

Heavy gold · Natural diamonds

Cuban links, with or without diamonds

Bring your heavy chains, bracelets and complete jewelry pieces. We consider the gold and any natural diamonds as part of the evaluation, including substantial pieces and larger collections.

Explore the gold bracelet guide ↗

Understand the metal

10K, 14K, 18K, 22K and 24K gold

Karat describes the proportion of gold in an alloy. It is different from the carat weight used for diamonds. A stamp helps identify a piece, but plating, solder, repairs and mixed components can affect what is present.

Nominal gold content by karat
MarkingApproximate gold proportionWhat to understand
10K41.7%10 parts gold out of 24
14K58.3%Often marked 585
18K75%Often marked 750
22K91.7%A higher gold proportion, still an alloy
24KNear-pure goldConfirm the stated fineness and actual item

These are purity references, not prices or guaranteed test results. Gold-plated and gold-filled items differ from solid karat gold. See the World Gold Council's explanation of gold purity and our 14K gold value guide.

An item-specific offer

How is a cash-for-gold offer determined?

For scrap gold, a useful starting point is the weight of the gold-bearing metal multiplied by its verified gold proportion and a current pure-gold price per unit of weight. This estimates metal value; it is not a guaranteed purchase price.

Spot gold is a market reference for gold itself. Jewelry's total weight may include stones, springs or other non-gold parts. Keep grams and troy ounces consistent when comparing calculations. Our gold valuation guide explains the distinction.

A purchase offer can differ from theoretical metal value because of recovery or refining costs, resale potential, market conditions and the buyer's margin. Designer provenance, collectible coin features and natural diamonds need separate consideration. Ask for the final net amount and the factors behind it.

  1. Identify and examine the items

    Markings, construction, maker details and condition help establish what is being evaluated. A photograph or receipt can assist but does not replace inspecting the piece.

  2. Check purity and weight

    Ask how purity is tested, which parts are included in the weight and whether stones or non-gold components affect the calculation. Mixed karats should not be treated as one assumed purity.

  3. Review the purchase terms

    Compare the offer, any deductions and payment arrangements. A retail replacement appraisal, an online asking price and a purchase offer serve different purposes.

What should you know about gold testing?

Evaluation may involve reading hallmarks, examining construction and choosing a testing method suited to the item. X-ray fluorescence (XRF) analyzes metal composition, but plating can affect the result. Acid or touchstone testing uses a sample or streak. Neither a marking nor one surface reading should be treated as the whole evaluation.

Ask which method will be used on your piece and whether it could leave a mark or require a sample. Discuss that first, especially for collectible coins, inherited jewelry or signed pieces. Call before visiting if you have testing concerns.

For background, GIA explains touchstone testing and how plating can affect XRF results.

Compare estimates carefully

A phone estimate can change after inspection

A preliminary phone or photo estimate uses details that have not yet been verified. The final in-person offer may be higher or lower after purity, weight, condition, authenticity, stones, maker details and other characteristics are checked. Market prices can also move before your visit.

Ask what assumptions an estimate uses, what remains to be checked and whether the amount is the final net purchase offer. There is no obligation to sell simply because you request an evaluation.

Discuss your gold ↗

Prepare for your visit

What should you bring when selling gold?

  • The complete jewelry, coins or collection you want evaluated.
  • Receipts, certificates, grading reports, original holders or packaging you already have.
  • Information about repairs, modifications, maker marks or inherited ownership.
  • Identification and relevant ownership or estate documents; call to confirm what is needed for your transaction.
  • Your questions about testing, payment method and timing.

Missing paperwork does not establish that an item has no value. Bring what you have. Do not clean collectible coins, remove gemstones or repair jewelry solely for the evaluation without discussing it first.

Visit the Downtown Los Angeles Jewelry District

617 S. Hill Street
Los Angeles, CA 90014

Call 310-663-1340 or arrange an appointment before traveling to confirm availability. Discuss the size of your collection, building access and parking arrangements when planning your visit.

Get directions ↗

Cash, bank wire and business check are available for agreed purchases. Confirm timing and payment requirements before accepting an offer.

Questions about selling gold in Los Angeles

Where can I sell gold in Los Angeles?

html:
Website Privacy Information

This notice explains information processed through the Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds website when you browse, contact us or use available website features.

Browsing and website security

Cloudflare helps deliver and protect this website. It processes technical request information, which can include your IP address and browser information, to provide hosting and security. If an online inquiry form is available, Cloudflare Turnstile checks for automated abuse before a message can be sent. See Cloudflare's privacy information.

This website does not offer customer account registration, a newsletter signup or an on-site payment form.

Contacting the business

You choose what to share when you call or email us. When an online inquiry form is available, it asks for your name, email address, item type and message. A phone number is optional. The form asks permission to use those details to respond to your inquiry; that permission is not a signup for marketing.

When available, the online form uses Resend to forward accepted inquiries to the business mailbox. The message includes the contact details and description you provide, along with a reference number. See Resend's privacy information. A message accepted by the email service is not a guarantee of inbox receipt or an appointment confirmation.

Do not include identification documents, banking information, payment-card details or other sensitive material in a website inquiry. The form does not accept file uploads. Ask the business how to provide any documents needed for a particular transaction.

Optional analytics

If Google Analytics is enabled on this website, Privacy preferences lets you choose whether to allow it. The website does not load its optional Google Analytics script before you allow analytics. Calling, emailing, opening an appointment link and sending an available inquiry do not require analytics consent.

When you allow analytics, it helps the business understand page visits and contact actions. The website's own contact-action events include the action and the site page, without the name, email address, phone number or message entered in the inquiry form. Google can also process browser, device and cookie information. See Google's privacy policy.

These website analytics controls keep advertising storage and personalized advertising off. Opening an appointment link is measured as a click, not a confirmed booking; a form acceptance is not measured as confirmed inbox delivery.

Changing your browser preferences

Open Privacy preferences to change or withdraw your analytics choice. Rejecting optional analytics keeps it off. Withdrawing an earlier permission disables optional analytics on the current page and clears the accessible analytics cookies used by this setup. When the saved choice can be updated or removed, the page reloads to stop the loaded analytics script. If browser storage prevents both, analytics stays off on the current page and a notice explains that the choice applies only to that page. You can remove the earlier saved choice in your browser settings.

Your saved analytics choice is valid for up to 180 days. After it expires, analytics stays off until you choose to allow it again. If browser storage is unavailable, the page explains that your choice applies only to that page. You can also remove this site's saved browser data using your browser settings.

The menu can separately remember whether you choose sounds on or off. This preference does not require your name or contact details. Change it using the menu sound control or clear this site's saved browser data.

How long information is kept

We keep customer inquiries only as long as needed to answer questions and complete transactions, and we delete them upon request. All privacy and deletion requests are handled by the owner.

The 180-day analytics preference period describes how long a saved permission remains valid. It does not describe how long inquiry messages, business records or service-provider data are retained, and it does not automatically delete the saved browser record.

Appointment links and other services

Phone and email links open your device's calling or email service. Appointment links can open Calendly, where you choose the information to provide. Review Calendly's privacy notice before using its scheduling service.

Maps, social profiles and other external links take you to services with their own privacy practices. The contact choices on this website do not change the privacy settings of those services.

Questions and requests

To ask about information you have shared with Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds, or to request a correction or removal, email cash4goldanddiamond@gmail.com, call 310-663-1340, or write to 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014. Describe your request and the contact method you used. Do not send unnecessary sensitive documents.

No single visual check can authenticate a Rolex. Weight, a serial number, dial printing or hand motion may raise questions, but the complete watch and its configuration need an appropriate physical examination.

In this guide

  • Use photographs to identify questions
  • Do not rely on simple pass-or-fail tests
  • Distinguish different kinds of replacement
  • Match records to the actual item
  • Agree on a suitable examination
  • If you are considering a sale

Use photographs to identify questions

Compare the claimed reference with reliable manufacturer information, but do not assume that a current catalog contains every older configuration. Ask about an apparent mismatch instead of declaring a watch genuine or counterfeit from one feature.

A photograph may hide movement details, later parts or damage. A familiar-looking dial does not authenticate the whole timepiece, and an unusual configuration may require historical research.

Do not rely on simple pass-or-fail tests

Weight varies with material, bracelet length and configuration. Hand motion, lens appearance and engraving cannot independently establish authenticity. A copied identifying number can appear convincing while proving nothing about the item carrying it.

Water resistance is not an authenticity test. Never immerse a watch to find out whether it is genuine. Do not scratch metal, force controls or use improvised tools to expose numbers or remove components.

Distinguish different kinds of replacement

Ask separately about original components, manufacturer service replacements, aftermarket parts and suspected counterfeit components. A later part does not automatically explain the status of every other part in the watch.

For a vintage example, the vintage Rolex guide covers records and originality. For gem-set watches, a diamond bezel also raises separate questions about stone identity and the source of the setting; see the diamond watch guide.

Match records to the actual item

Bring warranty papers, purchase records and service invoices. Check that their descriptions and identifying information correspond to the watch. A box or card alone is not proof of authenticity.

Record known repairs and explain missing history honestly. Do not buy unrelated paperwork to make a watch appear to have documented provenance.

Agree on a suitable examination

Ask the professional what will be examined, whether the case must be opened, what conclusions can be documented and what limitations remain. Give permission before proposed work and obtain an item record if the watch must be left.

Rolex provides official servicing information. Its Certified Pre-Owned programme is a specific brand programme; an independent purchase evaluation is not automatically a Rolex-issued guarantee or a formal authentication report.

If you are considering a sale

Use the Rolex selling checklist to organize the complete watch and accessories. Raise authenticity concerns before discussing a final purchase amount, and do not present an uncertain watch as authenticated.

Contact Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014, or call 310-663-1340 to arrange an evaluation. Cash, bank wire and business check are available for agreed purchases; confirm the payment arrangements before accepting.

html:
For gold jewelry with diamonds, describe the complete piece and provide matching stone reports if available. A photograph or report can inform an enquiry, but the buyer still needs to assess the actual jewelry. Confirm evaluation, shipping and return arrangements before sending valuables.

In this guide

  • Describe the jewelry and its components together
  • Match each report to the relevant stone
  • Keep gold weight and diamond information separate
  • Agree on receiving and return arrangements
  • Review the offer for the exact items sent
  • Discuss your collection with Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds

Describe the jewelry and its components together

Identify whether you have a ring, necklace, Cuban chain, bracelet or mixed collection. Include known metal markings, approximate dimensions, visible damage and any replaced parts. Clear photographs can help the buyer understand the enquiry without establishing authenticity or final value.

Keep the actual piece intact while discussing the process. Removing stones simply to reduce the item to metal can damage jewelry or lose useful information about the complete design.

Match each report to the relevant stone

Bring or send the information requested by the buyer from any existing grading report. Keep reports distinguishable when a collection contains several diamonds. GIA explains the diamond quality factors used to describe stones; weight alone does not establish a purchase amount.

State what is known and what is uncertain, including whether a stone has been identified as natural or laboratory-grown. Do not guess grades or origin from appearance. Our 4Cs guide explains the terminology.

Keep gold weight and diamond information separate

A scale reading for diamond jewelry includes the mounted stones and may include other components. Ask how the net alloy weight and any estimated stone weights are handled. The offer may concern the complete piece rather than separate amounts for every component.

Ask what the final total includes without adding an intact-jewelry estimate to the full separate value of the same materials. Our gold valuation guide explains this distinction.

Agree on receiving and return arrangements

Before mailing, confirm that the buyer accepts your item type, obtain current receiving instructions, and review coverage, packaging and return terms. A carrier's declared-value guidance is specific to that service and does not establish another company's coverage.

Keep an inventory, photographs, acceptance receipt and appropriate proof of value. USPS claim requirements illustrate why those records matter. See our mail-in gold checklist for questions to resolve before dispatch.

Review the offer for the exact items sent

Confirm which stones, jewelry and accessories are included. Ask about outstanding checks, any proposed alteration, charges, offer validity and the way you accept or decline. If the offer differs from an initial estimate, request the reasons.

Agree on payment method and timing before completing the sale. Do not assume an older article's turnaround time or payment list describes the current arrangement.

Discuss your collection with Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds

Call 310-663-1340 or contact us about gold jewelry and Cuban chains with or without diamonds. Single pieces and large collections are welcome. In-person evaluations are available at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014, with cash, bank wire or business-check payment.

Plan your evaluation in Downtown Los Angeles

Bring your items and any reports, receipts, or service records you already have. Contact us to discuss selling diamonds in Los Angeles and arrange an evaluation.

Call 310-663-1340 ↗

heading: Gold Bars: Compare Dealer Quotes, Records and Resale Terms
description: Compare gold-bar quotes, premiums, assay records and resale terms. Prepare questions and existing records for a gold evaluation in Downtown Los Angeles.
html:
Compare gold bars by their stated weight and fineness, the records supplied with the exact bar, and the complete written purchase or resale quote. A dealer ranking, stamped logo or quoted spot price does not establish authenticity or the amount you will receive.

Compare the transaction, not a star rating

A useful comparison starts with the same bar and the same direction of trade. A dealer's retail selling price is different from its offer to buy your bar. Record the weight, refiner, stated fineness, packaging and serial number where present, then ask for an itemized quote. Compare quotes close together in time because the underlying gold market can change.

The CFTC's questions for precious-metal buyers explain why the spread between purchase and resale prices matters. Ask about premiums, commissions, shipping, storage and any other charges that apply to your transaction. An attractive headline price is not a complete quote.

Keep copies of the written terms. A quote should make clear whether the amount is final, subject to examination, or dependent on a particular payment method. When comparing a local visit with an online transaction, include delivery arrangements, the examination process, return terms and who is responsible for the item at each stage.

What the bar and its records can tell you

Bring the bar with its original packaging, assay card, receipt and any prior transaction records that you already have. Match identifying details across those records instead of assuming that a card belongs to the nearby bar. Do not open sealed packaging or alter a bar just to prepare it for an initial conversation.

Records help establish what is being offered, but a photograph, logo or stated purity is not conclusive authentication. Ask the evaluator which checks are appropriate and whether any proposed test would alter the item. The LBMA's physical-market guidelines describe limitations of different testing techniques; no single casual home check should be treated as a definitive result.

Understand the limits of a Good Delivery claim

LBMA Good Delivery is a defined wholesale-market standard. The LBMA explains that its lists cover specified large wholesale bars, and that other refined products made by an accredited refiner are outside that listing's scope. A small retail bar is not automatically a London Good Delivery bar because its maker appears on a list.

Likewise, a dealer's description of its own service should be supported by evidence relevant to that claim. The World Gold Council's Gold Dealer Assurance Standard provides context for retail-dealer assurance. A link to that standard is not evidence that a particular shop holds certification.

Keep bullion and collectible value separate

Bars and coins can require different evaluation questions. For coins, record the issue, date, denomination, condition and existing holder information; a possible collectible component should not be assumed from metal content alone. For a mixed collection, ask the evaluator to explain which pieces are being considered for bullion value and which may need closer identification.

Our Downtown Los Angeles gold-coin guide explains how to prepare a collection. If jewelry is included, keep it separate from bars and coins so the discussion of gold weight and purity stays clear.

Prepare a Downtown Los Angeles evaluation

Contact Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds before transporting a valuable collection. Describe the items, approximate quantities and available records, and confirm the arrangements for a visit. The business is at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014. Gold jewelry, scrap gold, heavy Cuban chains, and gold and silver coins are part of the gold-buying service; discuss your specific bars before making a trip.

Cash, bank wire and business check are available for agreed purchases. Confirm the method and timing for your particular transaction before accepting an offer. This page does not quote a current gold price, guarantee a payout or identify products currently held for sale.

Questions about comparing gold bars

Does a smaller gold bar always cost less per gram?

Compare the full quoted cost per unit of fine gold for the products under consideration. A smaller total purchase amount does not by itself establish a lower premium or better resale outcome.

Is an assay card enough to establish authenticity?

No. Keep it with the corresponding item and ask how the bar, identifying details and records will be checked together. The appropriate examination depends on the item and circumstances.

Which dealer should I choose?

Compare documented terms, relevant evaluation experience and the process for your exact transaction. This guide does not assign unverified ratings to Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds or competing businesses.

  • CFTC: questions before buying physical metals
  • LBMA: physical-market testing guidelines
  • LBMA: scope of Good Delivery
  • World Gold Council: dealer assurance

Related guides

  • How gold is valued

Keep the complete items and existing records together. Arrange an evaluation at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014, or call 310-663-1340.

Compare a jewelry buyer’s offer for the complete item, the factors used in the evaluation, any fees and the proposed payment timing. A purchase offer, a consignment estimate and an insurance appraisal answer different questions. Keep the pieces intact and bring existing records so each discussion starts with the same information.

Compare the same items and transaction terms

A Los Angeles jewelry collection can include a heavy gold bracelet, a diamond ring, inherited pieces and a luxury watch. One total price gives you little information about how those different items were considered. Ask for a breakdown that lets you distinguish metal, stones and any value assigned to the complete piece. Record the date and any conditions attached to the offer.

Describe the same items to each prospective buyer. Include known repairs, missing components, altered settings and the records you have. An estimate made from a photograph or phone description can change after inspection. Treat it as an initial discussion rather than a commitment to pay an exact amount.

Before arranging a visit, confirm that the business buys the particular items you want to sell. A store that buys gold by weight may have a different process for an intact signed piece, while a watch discussion may depend on its reference, originality and service history. Ask how the complete item will be considered before allowing any disassembly.

Six options to discuss before choosing a buyer

OptionWhat to clarify
Direct jewelry buyerWhich pieces are included, the offer breakdown and when an agreed purchase is paid.
Precious-metal buyerHow weight and fineness are established, and how stones or non-gold parts are treated.
Estate-jewelry specialistWhether the proposal is a purchase or consignment, and which design or provenance details matter.
Independent appraiserThe appraisal’s purpose, fees and whether it is separate from any purchase proposal.
Consignment sellerCommission, custody, insurance, payment after sale and return arrangements if the item does not sell.
Pawn businessWhether you are discussing an outright sale or a loan, and the written terms of that specific transaction.

These are different services, not a ranking of individual businesses. Request the relevant terms from the operator you are considering rather than assuming that a category guarantees a higher offer, quicker payment or a particular level of expertise. Compare the amount you would receive after disclosed charges with the timing and obligations you would accept.

Separate gold characteristics from gemstone information

Bring hallmarks, receipts and any existing records, but leave the jewelry intact. The FTC’s precious-metal jewelry guide explains distinctions among gold fineness and plated products. Those descriptions help you prepare questions; a visible stamp alone does not establish what an individual purchase offer should be.

For a mounted diamond, ask what can be assessed while the stone is in its setting and whether additional examination is proposed. A grading report records characteristics; it is not a promise of a resale price. GIA describes the 4Cs as color, clarity, cut and carat weight. Bring an existing report so the item and its identifying details can be discussed together.

Bring records without confusing their purpose

Keep available receipts, grading reports, prior appraisals, original boxes and watch papers with the corresponding pieces. Records can provide context, but different documents serve different purposes. An insurance replacement appraisal is not the same as an immediate purchase offer for a used item.

GIA’s jewelry-selling guidance discusses appraisals and alternative selling routes. If you need an appraisal for insurance, tax, estate or another formal purpose, tell the appraiser what the document must address. Do not assume that a buyer’s informal evaluation fulfills that requirement.

For inherited jewelry, avoid polishing, dismantling or discarding components before a discussion about the whole piece. Keep any maker’s packaging or documentation you already have. If there are several items, make a simple list and photographs for your own records so you can keep track of the pieces being considered.

Questions to ask about an offer

  • Does the offer cover the complete piece, or only particular materials?
  • Which weights, markings, stone characteristics and condition observations were considered?
  • Are any fees or deductions included, and what net amount is proposed?

Keep the answers with the offer. A comparison is most useful when you can identify the same items, the same scope and the same conditions. You can take time to consider whether the proposed transaction suits you.

Natural cut and polished diamonds may be loose or mounted; rough and lab-grown diamonds are outside the buying scope.

Cash, bank wire and business check are available for agreed purchases; confirm the method and timing for your transaction. Contact the team before your visit to discuss your items and appointment arrangements.

Questions about selling jewelry

Can I discuss inherited jewelry without a grading report?

Yes. Bring the complete pieces and any records you have. Explain what is known and unknown about the items; a report is useful context, but its absence does not prevent an initial discussion.

Is same-day payment guaranteed?

No timing should be assumed from an article or phone estimate. Confirm an accepted offer, the payment method and the expected timing for that transaction before proceeding.

Should an intact gold piece be treated only as scrap?

Ask how the complete piece is being considered before deciding. Its condition, design, components and identifying records may be relevant to the buyer’s assessment; a metal-only estimate and an offer for the intact item are different proposals.
